field.name: DELAY
field.description: Main Clock turn on delay for Deep Sleep wake up

field.name: FORCEWAKE
field.description: Force peripheral clocking to stay on during deep-sleep mode. When 1, clocking to peripherals is prevented from being shut down when the CPU enters deep-sleep mode. This is intended to allow a coprocessor to continue operating while the main CPU(s) are shut down.

field.name: FCWAKE
field.description: Wake for Flexcomm Interfaces. When 1, any Flexcomm Interface FIFO reaching the level specified by its own TXLVL will cause peripheral clocking to wake up temporarily while the related status is asserted.

field.name: DMICWAKE
field.description: Wake for Digital Microphone. When 1, the digital microphone input FIFO reaching the level specified by TRIGLVL of either channel will cause peripheral clocking to wake up temporarily while the related status is asserted.

field.name: DMAC0WAKE
field.description: Wake for DMAC0. When 1, DMAC0 being busy will cause peripheral clocking to remain running until DMAC0 completes. This is generally used in conjunction with bit 1 and/or 2 in order to prevent peripheral clocking from being shut down as soon as the cause of wake-up is cleared, but before DMAC0 has completed its related activity.

field.name: DMAC1WAKE
field.description: Wake for DMAC1. When 1, DMAC1 being busy will cause peripheral clocking to remain running until DMAC1 completes. This is generally used in conjunction with bit 1 and/or 2 in order to prevent peripheral clocking from being shut down as soon as the cause of wake-up is cleared, but before DMAC1 has completed its related activity.

field.name: ESPIWAKE
field.description: Wake for ESPI. When 1, ESPI being busy will cause peripheral clocking to remain running until ESPI completes. This is generally used in conjunction with bit 1 and/or 2 in order to prevent peripheral clocking from being shut down as soon as the cause of wake-up is cleared, but before ESPI has completed its related activity.

field.description: A 256-bit random number set by boot ROM on each restart

field.name: BOOTSTATEHMAC

field.name: ZEROIZE
field.description: Zeroize. Begin Zeroize operation for Quiddikey and go to Error state

field.name: GENERATEKEY
field.description: Set Intrinsic Key. Begin Set Intrinsic Key operation

field.name: SETKEY
field.description: Set Key. Begin Set User Key operation

field.name: GETKEY
field.description: Get Key. Begin Get Key operation

field.name: KEYIDX
field.description: Key index for Set Key operations

field.name: KEYSIZE
field.description: Key Size for Set Key operations

field.name: READYEN
field.description: Enable corresponding interrupt in STAT, which indicates that the initialization or a operation is completed.

field.name: SUCCESEN
field.description: Enable corresponding interrupt in STAT, which indicates last operation was successful.

field.name: ERROREN
field.description: Enable corresponding interrupt in STAT, which indicates that PUF is in the error state and no operations can be performed.

field.name: KEYINREQEN
field.description: Enable corresponding interrupt in STAT, which is request for next part of key.

field.name: KEYOUTAVAILEN
field.description: Enable corresponding interrupt in STAT, which is next part of key is available.

field.name: CODEINREQEN
field.description: Enable corresponding interrupt in STAT, which is request for next part of AC/KC.

field.name: CODEOUTAVAILEN
field.description: Enable corresponding interrupt in STAT, which is next part of AC/KC is available.

field.name: BLOCKENROLL_SETKEY
field.description: Block Enroll and Set Key Operation

register.name: MOD
register.description: Watchdog mode register. This register contains the basic mode and status of the Watchdog Timer.

field.name: WDEN
field.description: Watchdog enable bit. Once this bit is set to one and a watchdog feed is performed, the watchdog timer will run permanently.

enumeratedValue.name: STOP
enumeratedValue.description: Stop. The watchdog timer is stopped.

enumeratedValue.name: RUN
enumeratedValue.description: Run. The watchdog timer is running.

field.name: WDRESET
field.description: Watchdog reset enable bit. Once this bit has been written with a 1 it cannot be re-written with a 0.

enumeratedValue.name: INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: Interrupt. A watchdog time-out will not cause a chip reset.

enumeratedValue.name: RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Reset. A watchdog time-out will cause a chip reset.

field.name: WDTOF
field.description: Watchdog time-out flag. Set when the watchdog timer times out, by a feed error, or by events associated with WDPROTECT. Cleared by software writing a 0 to this bit position. Causes a chip reset if WDRESET = 1.

field.name: WDINT
field.description: Warning interrupt flag. Set when the timer is at or below the value in WDWARNINT. Cleared by software writing a 1 to this bit position. Note that this bit cannot be cleared while the WARNINT value is equal to the value of the TV register. This can occur if the value of WARNINT is 0 and the WDRESET bit is 0 when TV decrements to 0.

field.name: WDPROTECT
field.description: Watchdog update mode. This bit can be set once by software and is only cleared by a reset.

enumeratedValue.name: FLEXIBLE
enumeratedValue.description: Flexible. The watchdog time-out value (TC) can be changed at any time.

enumeratedValue.name: THRESHOLD
enumeratedValue.description: Threshold. The watchdog time-out value (TC) can be changed only after the counter is below the value of WDWARNINT and WDWINDOW.

field.name: LOCK
field.description: Once this bit is set to one and a watchdog feed is performed, disabling or powering down the watchdog oscillator is prevented by hardware. This bit can be set once by software and is only cleared by any reset.

register.name: TC
register.description: Watchdog timer constant register. This 24-bit register determines the time-out value.

register.name: FEED
register.description: Watchdog feed sequence register. Writing 0xAA followed by 0x55 to this register reloads the Watchdog timer with the value contained in TC.

field.name: FEED
field.description: Feed value should be 0xAA followed by 0x55.

register.name: TV
register.description: Watchdog timer value register. This 24-bit register reads out the current value of the Watchdog timer.

field.name: DELAYVAL
field.description: Tick interval value. The delay will be equal to DELAYVAL + 1 periods of the timer clock. The minimum usable value is 1, for a delay of 2 timer clocks. A value of 0 stops the timer.

field.name: REPEAT
field.description: Repeat delay. 0 = One-time delay. 1 = Delay repeats continuously.

field.name: INTR
field.description: Interrupt flag. 0 = No interrupt is pending. 1 = An interrupt is pending. A write of any value to this register clears this flag.

field.name: ACTIVE
field.description: Active flag. 0 = The Micro-Tick Timer is stopped. 1 = The Micro-Tick Timer is currently active.

field.name: CAPPOL0
field.description: Capture Polarity 0. 0 = Positive edge capture, 1 = Negative edge capture.

field.name: CAPPOL1
field.description: Capture Polarity 1. 0 = Positive edge capture, 1 = Negative edge capture.

field.name: CAPPOL2
field.description: Capture Polarity 2. 0 = Positive edge capture, 1 = Negative edge capture.

field.name: CAPPOL3
field.description: Capture Polarity 3. 0 = Positive edge capture, 1 = Negative edge capture.

field.name: CAPCLR0
field.description: Clear capture 0. Writing 1 to this bit clears the CAP0 register value.

field.name: CAPCLR1
field.description: Clear capture 1. Writing 1 to this bit clears the CAP1 register value.

field.name: CAPCLR2
field.description: Clear capture 2. Writing 1 to this bit clears the CAP2 register value.

field.name: CAPCLR3
field.description: Clear capture 3. Writing 1 to this bit clears the CAP3 register value.

field.name: CAP_VALUE
field.description: Capture value for the related capture event (UTICK_CAPn. Note: the value is 1 lower than the actual value of the Micro-tick Timer at the moment of the capture event.

field.name: VALID
field.description: Capture Valid. When 1, a value has been captured based on a transition of the related UTICK_CAPn pin. Cleared by writing to the related bit in the CAPCLR register.

enumeratedValue.name: POR_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: VDD POR event detected. (Writing a 1 to this bit clears this status).

enumeratedValue.name: RESET_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: ARM reset event detected. (Writing a 1 to this bit clears this status).

enumeratedValue.name: WDT0_RESET_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: WDT0 reset event detected. (Writing a 1 to this bit clears this status).

enumeratedValue.name: WDT1_RESET_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: WDT1 reset event detected. (Writing a 1 to this bit clears this status).

enumeratedValue.name: NONE
enumeratedValue.description: None, this may be selected in order to reduce power when no output is needed.

enumeratedValue.name: PROGRAMMED_CLK
enumeratedValue.description: PFD output is PFD programmed clock.

enumeratedValue.name: BYPASS
enumeratedValue.description: PFD output is AUDIOPLL0 reference input clock. (Bypass Mode)

field.name: LOCKTIMEDIV2
field.description: AUDIOPLL0 Lock Time Divide by 2: Programmed lock time is in uS (micro-seconds) and is programmed as half the actual lock time value.

field.name: NUM
field.description: This field contains the numerator of the AUDIOPLL0 fractional loop divider. NOTES: 1. The value of numerator must always be configured to be less than the value of the denominator. 2. The AUDIOPLL0NUM register can only be changed when the AUDIOPLL0 is disabled.

field.name: DENOM
field.description: This field contains the denominator of the AUDIOPLL0 fractional loop divider. NOTES: 1. The value of numerator must always be configured to be less than the value of the denominator. 2. The AUDIOPLL0DENOM register can only be changed when the AUDIOPLL0 is disabled.

field.name: PFD0
field.description: PLL Fractional Divider 0: Controls the fractional divider value. Valid PFD values are decimal 12-35.

field.name: PFD0_CLKRDY
field.description: PFD0 Clock Ready Status Flag: Read as 1 clock ready. Cleared by writing a 1.

field.name: PFD0_CLKGATE
field.description: PFD0 Clock Gate: 0: PFD0 clock is not gated. 1: PFD0 clock is gated

field.name: PFD1
field.description: PLL Fractional Divider 1: Controls the fractional divider value. Valid PFD values are decimal 12-35.

field.name: PFD1_CLKRDY
field.description: PFD1 Clock Ready Status Flag: Read as 1 clock ready. Cleared by writing a 1.

field.name: PFD1_CLKGATE
field.description: PFD1 Clock Gate: 0: PFD1 clock is not gated. 1: PFD1 clock is gated.

field.name: PFD2
field.description: PLL Fractional Divider 2: Controls the fractional divider value. Valid PFD values are decimal 12-35.

field.name: PFD2_CLKRDY
field.description: PFD2 Clock Ready Status Flag: Read as 1 clock ready. Cleared by writing a 1.

field.name: PFD2_CLKGATE
field.description: PFD2 Clock Gate: 0: PFD2 clock is not gated. 1: PFD2 clock is gated.

field.name: PFD3
field.description: PLL Fractional Divider 3: Controls the fractional divider value. Valid PFD values are decimal 12-35.

field.name: PFD3_CLKRDY
field.description: PFD3 Clock Ready Status Flag: Read as 1 clock ready. Cleared by writing a 1.

field.name: PFD3_CLKGATE
field.description: PFD3 Clock Gate: 0: PFD3 clock is not gated. 1: PFD3 clock is gated.

field.name: DIV
field.description: Clock Divider Value Selection. . . 0: Divide by 1. ... 255: Divide by 256.

field.name: RESET
field.description: Resets the divider counter. Can be used to make sure a new divider value is used right away rather than completing the previous count.

field.name: HALT
field.description: Halts the divider counter. The intent is to allow the divider's clock source to be changed without the risk of a glitch at the output.

field.name: REQFLAG
field.description: Divider status flag. Set when a change is made to the divider value, cleared when the change is complete.

enumeratedValue.name: PULSE_RXEV_HIGH

peripheral.name: PINT
peripheral.description: LPC-Next0 Pin interrupt and pattern match (PINT)

field.name: PMODE
field.description: Selects the interrupt mode for each pin interrupt. Bit n configures the pin interrupt selected in PINTSELn. 0 = Edge sensitive 1 = Level sensitive

register.name: IENR
register.description: Pin interrupt level or rising edge interrupt enable register

field.name: ENRL
field.description: Enables the rising edge or level interrupt for each pin interrupt. Bit n configures the pin interrupt selected in PINTSELn. 0 = Disable rising edge or level interrupt. 1 = Enable rising edge or level interrupt.

register.name: SIENR
register.description: Pin interrupt level or rising edge interrupt set register

field.name: SETENRL
field.description: Ones written to this address set bits in the IENR, thus enabling interrupts. Bit n sets bit n in the IENR register. 0 = No operation. 1 = Enable rising edge or level interrupt.

register.name: CIENR
register.description: Pin interrupt level (rising edge interrupt) clear register

field.name: CENRL
field.description: Ones written to this address clear bits in the IENR, thus disabling the interrupts. Bit n clears bit n in the IENR register. 0 = No operation. 1 = Disable rising edge or level interrupt.

register.name: IENF
register.description: Pin interrupt active level or falling edge interrupt enable register

field.name: ENAF
field.description: Enables the falling edge or configures the active level interrupt for each pin interrupt. Bit n configures the pin interrupt selected in PINTSELn. 0 = Disable falling edge interrupt or set active interrupt level LOW. 1 = Enable falling edge interrupt enabled or set active interrupt level HIGH.

register.name: SIENF
register.description: Pin interrupt active level or falling edge interrupt set register

field.name: SETENAF
field.description: Ones written to this address set bits in the IENF, thus enabling interrupts. Bit n sets bit n in the IENF register. 0 = No operation. 1 = Select HIGH-active interrupt or enable falling edge interrupt.

register.name: CIENF
register.description: Pin interrupt active level or falling edge interrupt clear register

field.name: CENAF
field.description: Ones written to this address clears bits in the IENF, thus disabling interrupts. Bit n clears bit n in the IENF register. 0 = No operation. 1 = LOW-active interrupt selected or falling edge interrupt disabled.

field.name: RDET
field.description: Rising edge detect. Bit n detects the rising edge of the pin selected in PINTSELn. Read 0: No rising edge has been detected on this pin since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit. Write 0: no operation. Read 1: a rising edge has been detected since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit. Write 1: clear rising edge detection for this pin.

field.name: FDET
field.description: Falling edge detect. Bit n detects the falling edge of the pin selected in PINTSELn. Read 0: No falling edge has been detected on this pin since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit. Write 0: no operation. Read 1: a falling edge has been detected since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit. Write 1: clear falling edge detection for this pin.

field.name: PSTAT
field.description: Pin interrupt status. Bit n returns the status, clears the edge interrupt, or inverts the active level of the pin selected in PINTSELn. Read 0: interrupt is not being requested for this interrupt pin. Write 0: no operation. Read 1: interrupt is being requested for this interrupt pin. Write 1 (edge-sensitive): clear rising- and falling-edge detection for this pin. Write 1 (level-sensitive): switch the active level for this pin (in the IENF register).

field.name: SEL_PMATCH
field.description: Specifies whether the 8 pin interrupts are controlled by the pin interrupt function or by the pattern match function.

enumeratedValue.name: PIN_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: Pin interrupt. Interrupts are driven in response to the standard pin interrupt function.

enumeratedValue.name: PATTERN_MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: Pattern match. Interrupts are driven in response to pattern matches.

field.name: ENA_RXEV
field.description: Enables the RXEV output to the CPU and/or to a GPIO output when the specified boolean expression evaluates to true.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. RXEV output to the CPU is disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. RXEV output to the CPU is enabled.

field.name: PMAT
field.description: This field displays the current state of pattern matches. A 1 in any bit of this field indicates that the corresponding product term is matched by the current state of the appropriate inputs.

field.name: PROD_ENDPTS0
field.description: Determines whether slice 0 is an endpoint.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_EFFECT
enumeratedValue.description: No effect. Slice 0 is not an endpoint.

enumeratedValue.name: ENDPOINT
enumeratedValue.description: endpoint. Slice 0 is the endpoint of a product term (minterm). Pin interrupt 0 in the NVIC is raised if the minterm evaluates as true.

field.name: CFG0
field.description: Specifies the match contribution condition for bit slice 0.

enumeratedValue.name: CONSTANT_HIGH
enumeratedValue.description: Constant HIGH. This bit slice always contributes to a product term match.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_RISING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky rising edge. Match occurs if a rising edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This bit is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky falling edge. Match occurs if a falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This bit is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_RISING_FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs if either a rising or falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This bit is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: HIGH_LEVEL
enumeratedValue.description: High level. Match (for this bit slice) occurs when there is a high level on the input specified for this bit slice in the PMSRC register.

enumeratedValue.name: LOW_LEVEL
enumeratedValue.description: Low level. Match occurs when there is a low level on the specified input.

enumeratedValue.name: CONSTANT_ZERO
enumeratedValue.description: Constant 0. This bit slice never contributes to a match (should be used to disable any unused bit slices).

enumeratedValue.name: EVENT
enumeratedValue.description: Event. Non-sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs on an event - i.e. when either a rising or falling edge is first detected on the specified input (this is a non-sticky version of value 0x3) . This bit is cleared after one clock cycle.

register.name: IR
register.description: Interrupt Register. The IR can be written to clear interrupts. The IR can be read to identify which of eight possible interrupt sources are pending.

field.name: CR0INT
field.description: Interrupt flag for capture channel 0 event.

field.name: CR1INT
field.description: Interrupt flag for capture channel 1 event.

field.name: CR2INT
field.description: Interrupt flag for capture channel 2 event.

field.name: CR3INT
field.description: Interrupt flag for capture channel 3 event.

register.name: TCR
register.description: Timer Control Register. The TCR is used to control the Timer Counter functions. The Timer Counter can be disabled or reset through the TCR.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The Timer Counter and Prescale Counter are enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The Timer Counter and the Prescale Counter are synchronously reset on the next positive edge of the APB bus clock. The counters remain reset until TCR[1] is returned to zero.

register.name: TC
register.description: Timer Counter. The 32 bit TC is incremented every PR+1 cycles of the APB bus clock. The TC is controlled through the TCR.

register.name: PR
register.description: Prescale Register. When the Prescale Counter (PC) is equal to this value, the next clock increments the TC and clears the PC.

register.name: PC
register.description: Prescale Counter. The 32 bit PC is a counter which is incremented to the value stored in PR. When the value in PR is reached, the TC is incremented and the PC is cleared. The PC is observable and controllable through the bus interface.

register.name: MCR
register.description: Match Control Register. The MCR is used to control if an interrupt is generated and if the TC is reset when a Match occurs.

field.name: MR0I
field.description: Interrupt on MR0: an interrupt is generated when MR0 matches the value in the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR0R
field.description: Reset on MR0: the TC will be reset if MR0 matches it. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR0S
field.description: Stop on MR0: the TC and PC will be stopped and TCR[0] will be set to 0 if MR0 matches the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR1I
field.description: Interrupt on MR1: an interrupt is generated when MR1 matches the value in the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR1R
field.description: Reset on MR1: the TC will be reset if MR1 matches it. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR1S
field.description: Stop on MR1: the TC and PC will be stopped and TCR[0] will be set to 0 if MR1 matches the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR2I
field.description: Interrupt on MR2: an interrupt is generated when MR2 matches the value in the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR2R
field.description: Reset on MR2: the TC will be reset if MR2 matches it. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR2S
field.description: Stop on MR2: the TC and PC will be stopped and TCR[0] will be set to 0 if MR2 matches the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR3I
field.description: Interrupt on MR3: an interrupt is generated when MR3 matches the value in the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR3R
field.description: Reset on MR3: the TC will be reset if MR3 matches it. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR3S
field.description: Stop on MR3: the TC and PC will be stopped and TCR[0] will be set to 0 if MR3 matches the TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR0RL
field.description: Reload MR0 with the contents of the Match 0 Shadow Register when the TC is reset to zero (either via a match event or a write to bit 1 of the TCR). 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR1RL
field.description: Reload MR1 with the contents of the Match 1 Shadow Register when the TC is reset to zero (either via a match event or a write to bit 1 of the TCR). 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR2RL
field.description: Reload MR2 with the contents of the Match 2 Shadow Register when the TC is reset to zero (either via a match event or a write to bit 1 of the TCR). 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: MR3RL
field.description: Reload MR3 with the contents of the Match 3 Shadow Register when the TC is reset to zero (either via a match event or a write to bit 1 of the TCR). 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

register.name: MR[%s]
register.description: Match Register . MR can be enabled through the MCR to reset the TC, stop both the TC and PC, and/or generate an interrupt every time MR matches the TC.

register.name: CCR
register.description: Capture Control Register. The CCR controls which edges of the capture inputs are used to load the Capture Registers and whether or not an interrupt is generated when a capture takes place.

field.name: CAP0RE
field.description: Rising edge of capture channel 0: a sequence of 0 then 1 causes CR0 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP0FE
field.description: Falling edge of capture channel 0: a sequence of 1 then 0 causes CR0 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP0I
field.description: Generate interrupt on channel 0 capture event: a CR0 load generates an interrupt.

field.name: CAP1RE
field.description: Rising edge of capture channel 1: a sequence of 0 then 1 causes CR1 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP1FE
field.description: Falling edge of capture channel 1: a sequence of 1 then 0 causes CR1 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP1I
field.description: Generate interrupt on channel 1 capture event: a CR1 load generates an interrupt.

field.name: CAP2RE
field.description: Rising edge of capture channel 2: a sequence of 0 then 1 causes CR2 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP2FE
field.description: Falling edge of capture channel 2: a sequence of 1 then 0 causes CR2 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP2I
field.description: Generate interrupt on channel 2 capture event: a CR2 load generates an interrupt.

field.name: CAP3RE
field.description: Rising edge of capture channel 3: a sequence of 0 then 1 causes CR3 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP3FE
field.description: Falling edge of capture channel 3: a sequence of 1 then 0 causes CR3 to be loaded with the contents of TC. 0 = disabled. 1 = enabled.

field.name: CAP3I
field.description: Generate interrupt on channel 3 capture event: a CR3 load generates an interrupt.

register.name: CR[%s]
register.description: Capture Register . CR is loaded with the value of TC when there is an event on the CAPn. input.

register.name: EMR
register.description: External Match Register. The EMR controls the match function and the external match pins.

field.name: EM0
field.description: External Match 0. This bit reflects the state of output MAT0, whether or not this output is connected to a pin. When a match occurs between the TC and MR0, this bit can either toggle, go LOW, go HIGH, or do nothing, as selected by EMR[5:4]. This bit is driven to the MAT pins if the match function is selected via IOCON. 0 = LOW. 1 = HIGH.

field.name: EM1
field.description: External Match 1. This bit reflects the state of output MAT1, whether or not this output is connected to a pin. When a match occurs between the TC and MR1, this bit can either toggle, go LOW, go HIGH, or do nothing, as selected by EMR[7:6]. This bit is driven to the MAT pins if the match function is selected via IOCON. 0 = LOW. 1 = HIGH.

field.name: EM2
field.description: External Match 2. This bit reflects the state of output MAT2, whether or not this output is connected to a pin. When a match occurs between the TC and MR2, this bit can either toggle, go LOW, go HIGH, or do nothing, as selected by EMR[9:8]. This bit is driven to the MAT pins if the match function is selected via IOCON. 0 = LOW. 1 = HIGH.

field.name: EM3
field.description: External Match 3. This bit reflects the state of output MAT3, whether or not this output is connected to a pin. When a match occurs between the TC and MR3, this bit can either toggle, go LOW, go HIGH, or do nothing, as selected by MR[11:10]. This bit is driven to the MAT pins if the match function is selected via IOCON. 0 = LOW. 1 = HIGH.

field.name: EMC0
field.description: External Match Control 0. Determines the functionality of External Match 0.

enumeratedValue.name: CLEAR
enumeratedValue.description: Clear. Clear the corresponding External Match bit/output to 0 (MAT0 pin is LOW if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: SET
enumeratedValue.description: Set. Set the corresponding External Match bit/output to 1 (MAT0 pin is HIGH if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: TOGGLE
enumeratedValue.description: Toggle. Toggle the corresponding External Match bit/output.

field.name: EMC1
field.description: External Match Control 1. Determines the functionality of External Match 1.

enumeratedValue.name: CLEAR
enumeratedValue.description: Clear. Clear the corresponding External Match bit/output to 0 (MAT1 pin is LOW if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: SET
enumeratedValue.description: Set. Set the corresponding External Match bit/output to 1 (MAT1 pin is HIGH if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: TOGGLE
enumeratedValue.description: Toggle. Toggle the corresponding External Match bit/output.

field.name: EMC2
field.description: External Match Control 2. Determines the functionality of External Match 2.

enumeratedValue.name: CLEAR
enumeratedValue.description: Clear. Clear the corresponding External Match bit/output to 0 (MAT2 pin is LOW if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: SET
enumeratedValue.description: Set. Set the corresponding External Match bit/output to 1 (MAT2 pin is HIGH if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: TOGGLE
enumeratedValue.description: Toggle. Toggle the corresponding External Match bit/output.

field.name: EMC3
field.description: External Match Control 3. Determines the functionality of External Match 3.

enumeratedValue.name: CLEAR
enumeratedValue.description: Clear. Clear the corresponding External Match bit/output to 0 (MAT3 pin is LOW if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: SET
enumeratedValue.description: Set. Set the corresponding External Match bit/output to 1 (MAT3 pin is HIGH if pinned out).

enumeratedValue.name: TOGGLE
enumeratedValue.description: Toggle. Toggle the corresponding External Match bit/output.

register.name: CTCR
register.description: Count Control Register. The CTCR selects between Timer and Counter mode, and in Counter mode selects the signal and edge(s) for counting.

field.name: CTMODE
field.description: Counter/Timer Mode This field selects which rising APB bus clock edges can increment Timer's Prescale Counter (PC), or clear PC and increment Timer Counter (TC). Timer Mode: the TC is incremented when the Prescale Counter matches the Prescale Register.

enumeratedValue.name: TIMER
enumeratedValue.description: Timer Mode. Incremented every rising APB bus clock edge.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTER_RISING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Counter Mode rising edge. TC is incremented on rising edges on the CAP input selected by bits 3:2.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTER_FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Counter Mode falling edge. TC is incremented on falling edges on the CAP input selected by bits 3:2.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTER_DUAL_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Counter Mode dual edge. TC is incremented on both edges on the CAP input selected by bits 3:2.

field.name: CINSEL
field.description: Count Input Select When bits 1:0 in this register are not 00, these bits select which CAP pin is sampled for clocking. Note: If Counter mode is selected for a particular CAPn input in the CTCR, the 3 bits for that input in the Capture Control Register (CCR) must be programmed as 000. However, capture and/or interrupt can be selected for the other 3 CAPn inputs in the same timer.

field.name: ENCC
field.description: Setting this bit to 1 enables clearing of the timer and the prescaler when the capture-edge event specified in bits 7:5 occurs.

field.name: SELCC
field.description: Edge select. When bit 4 is 1, these bits select which capture input edge will cause the timer and prescaler to be cleared. These bits have no effect when bit 4 is low. Values 0x2 to 0x3 and 0x6 to 0x7 are reserved.

enumeratedValue.name: CHANNEL_0_RISING
enumeratedValue.description: Channel 0 Rising Edge. Rising edge of the signal on capture channel 0 clears the timer (if bit 4 is set).

enumeratedValue.name: CHANNEL_0_FALLING
enumeratedValue.description: Channel 0 Falling Edge. Falling edge of the signal on capture channel 0 clears the timer (if bit 4 is set).

enumeratedValue.name: CHANNEL_1_RISING
enumeratedValue.description: Channel 1 Rising Edge. Rising edge of the signal on capture channel 1 clears the timer (if bit 4 is set).

enumeratedValue.name: CHANNEL_1_FALLING
enumeratedValue.description: Channel 1 Falling Edge. Falling edge of the signal on capture channel 1 clears the timer (if bit 4 is set).

enumeratedValue.name: CHANNEL_2_RISING
enumeratedValue.description: Channel 2 Rising Edge. Rising edge of the signal on capture channel 2 clears the timer (if bit 4 is set).

enumeratedValue.name: CHANNEL_2_FALLING
enumeratedValue.description: Channel 2 Falling Edge. Falling edge of the signal on capture channel 2 clears the timer (if bit 4 is set).

register.name: PWMC
register.description: PWM Control Register. The PWMCON enables PWM mode for the external match pins.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: Match. CTIMERn_MAT0 is controlled by EM0.

enumeratedValue.name: PWM
enumeratedValue.description: PWM. PWM mode is enabled for CTIMERn_MAT0.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: Match. CTIMERn_MAT01 is controlled by EM1.

enumeratedValue.name: PWM
enumeratedValue.description: PWM. PWM mode is enabled for CTIMERn_MAT1.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: Match. CTIMERn_MAT2 is controlled by EM2.

enumeratedValue.name: PWM
enumeratedValue.description: PWM. PWM mode is enabled for CTIMERn_MAT2.

field.name: PWMEN3
field.description: PWM mode enable for channel3. Note: It is recommended to use match channel 3 to set the PWM cycle.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: Match. CTIMERn_MAT3 is controlled by EM3.

enumeratedValue.name: PWM
enumeratedValue.description: PWM. PWM mode is enabled for CT132Bn_MAT3.

register.name: MSR[%s]
register.description: Match Shadow Register . If enabled, the Match Register will be automatically reloaded with the contents of this register whenever the TC is reset to zero.

cluster.name: CHANNEL[%s]
cluster.description: Array of registers: CTRL, INTVAL, STAT, TIMER

register.name: INTVAL
register.description: MRT Time interval value register. This value is loaded into the TIMER register.

field.name: IVALUE
field.description: Time interval load value. This value is loaded into the TIMERn register and the MRT channel n starts counting down from IVALUE -1. If the timer is idle, writing a non-zero value to this bit field starts the timer immediately. If the timer is running, writing a zero to this bit field does the following: If LOAD = 1, the timer stops immediately. If LOAD = 0, the timer stops at the end of the time interval.

field.name: LOAD
field.description: Determines how the timer interval value IVALUE -1 is loaded into the TIMERn register. This bit is write-only. Reading this bit always returns 0.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_FORCE_LOAD
enumeratedValue.description: No force load. The load from the INTVALn register to the TIMERn register is processed at the end of the time interval if the repeat mode is selected.

enumeratedValue.name: FORCE_LOAD
enumeratedValue.description: Force load. The INTVALn interval value IVALUE -1 is immediately loaded into the TIMERn register while TIMERn is running.

register.name: TIMER
register.description: MRT Timer register. This register reads the value of the down-counter.

field.name: VALUE
field.description: Holds the current timer value of the down-counter. The initial value of the TIMERn register is loaded as IVALUE - 1 from the INTVALn register either at the end of the time interval or immediately in the following cases: INTVALn register is updated in the idle state. INTVALn register is updated with LOAD = 1. When the timer is in idle state, reading this bit fields returns -1 (0x00FF FFFF).

register.name: CTRL
register.description: MRT Control register. This register controls the MRT modes.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_PENDING_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: No pending interrupt. Writing a zero is equivalent to no operation.

enumeratedValue.name: PENDING_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: Pending interrupt. The interrupt is pending because TIMERn has reached the end of the time interval. If the INTEN bit in the CONTROLn is also set to 1, the interrupt for timer channel n and the global interrupt are raised. Writing a 1 to this bit clears the interrupt request.

field.name: RUN
field.description: Indicates the state of TIMERn. This bit is read-only.

field.name: INUSE
field.description: Channel In Use flag. Operating details depend on the MULTITASK bit in the MODCFG register, and affects the use of IDLE_CH. See Idle channel register for details of the two operating modes.

enumeratedValue.name: NO
enumeratedValue.description: This channel is not in use.

register.name: MODCFG
register.description: Module Configuration register. This register provides information about this particular MRT instance, and allows choosing an overall mode for the idle channel feature.

field.name: NOC
field.description: Identifies the number of channels in this MRT.(4 channels on this device.)

field.name: NOB
field.description: Identifies the number of timer bits in this MRT. (24 bits wide on this device.)

field.name: MULTITASK
field.description: Selects the operating mode for the INUSE flags and the IDLE_CH register.

enumeratedValue.name: HARDWARE_STATUS_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Hardware status mode. In this mode, the INUSE(n) flags for all channels are reset.

register.name: IDLE_CH
register.description: Idle channel register. This register returns the number of the first idle channel.

field.name: CHAN
field.description: Idle channel. Reading the CHAN bits, returns the lowest idle timer channel. The number is positioned such that it can be used as an offset from the MRT base address in order to access the registers for the allocated channel. If all timer channels are running, CHAN = 0xF. See text above for more details.

field.name: GFLAG0
field.description: Monitors the interrupt flag of TIMER0.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_PENDING_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: No pending interrupt. Writing a zero is equivalent to no operation.

enumeratedValue.name: PENDING_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: Pending interrupt. The interrupt is pending because TIMER0 has reached the end of the time interval. If the INTEN bit in the CONTROL0 register is also set to 1, the interrupt for timer channel 0 and the global interrupt are raised. Writing a 1 to this bit clears the interrupt request.

field.name: GFLAG1
field.description: Monitors the interrupt flag of TIMER1. See description of channel 0.

field.name: GFLAG2
field.description: Monitors the interrupt flag of TIMER2. See description of channel 0.

field.name: GFLAG3
field.description: Monitors the interrupt flag of TIMER3. See description of channel 0.

enumeratedValue.name: CYCLE_DONE
enumeratedValue.description: Process complete. Measurement cycle is complete. The results are ready in the RESULT field.

enumeratedValue.name: IN_PROGRESS
enumeratedValue.description: In Progress. Measurement cycle is in progress.

enumeratedValue.name: FREQ_ME_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Frequency Measurement Mode. FREQMECTRL works in a Frequency Measurement mode. Once the measurement starts (real count start is aligned at rising edge arrival on reference clock), the target counter increments by the target clock until the reference counter running by the reference clock reaches the count end point selected by REF_SCALE.

enumeratedValue.name: PULSE_ME_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Pulse Width Measurement mode. FREQMECTRL works in a Pulse Width Measurement mode, measuring the high or low period of reference clock input selected by PULSE_POL. The target counter starts incrementing by the target clock once a corresponding trigger edge (rising edge for high period measurement and falling edge for low period) occurs.

enumeratedValue.name: HIGH_PERIOD
enumeratedValue.description: High Period. High period of reference clock is measured in Pulse Width Measurement mode triggered by the rising edge on the reference clock input.

enumeratedValue.name: LOW_PERIOD
enumeratedValue.description: Low Period. Low period of reference clock is measured in Pulse Width Measurement mode triggered by the falling edge on the reference clock input.

enumeratedValue.name: FORCE_TERMINATE
enumeratedValue.description: Force Terminate. Forces the termination of any measurement cycle currently in progress and resets RESULT or just resets RESULT if in idle.

enumeratedValue.name: INITIATE_A_FREQME_CYCLE
enumeratedValue.description: Initiates Measurement Cycle. Initiates frequency or pulse width measurement process. Hardware clears the MEASURE_IN_PROGRESS bit when the measurement cycle completes. A new measurement starts if there is an active measurement in progress.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_IN_RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Not in reset. The RTC is not held in reset. This bit must be cleared prior to configuring or initiating any operation of the RTC.

enumeratedValue.name: IN_RESET
enumeratedValue.description: In reset. The RTC is held in reset. All register bits within the RTC will be forced to their reset value except the RTC_OSC_PD bit. This bit must be cleared before writing to any register in the RTC - including writes to set any of the other bits within this register. Do not attempt to write to any bits of this register at the same time that the reset bit is being cleared.

field.name: ALARM1HZ
field.description: RTC 1 Hz timer alarm flag status.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: No match. No match has occurred on the 1 Hz RTC timer. Writing a 0 has no effect.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: Match. A match condition has occurred on the 1 Hz RTC timer. This flag generates an RTC alarm interrupt request RTC_ALARM which can also wake up the part from any low power mode. Writing a 1 clears this bit.

field.name: WAKE1KHZ
field.description: RTC 1 kHz timer wake-up flag status.

enumeratedValue.name: RUN
enumeratedValue.description: Run. The RTC 1 kHz timer is running. Writing a 0 has no effect.

enumeratedValue.name: TIME_OUT
enumeratedValue.description: Time-out. The 1 kHz high-resolution/wake-up timer has timed out. This flag generates an RTC wake-up interrupt request RTC-WAKE which can also wake up the part from any low power mode. Writing a 1 clears this bit.

field.name: ALARMDPD_EN
field.description: RTC 1 Hz timer alarm enable for Deep power-down.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disable. A match on the 1 Hz RTC timer will not bring the part out of Deep power-down mode.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. A match on the 1 Hz RTC timer bring the part out of Deep power-down mode.

field.name: WAKEDPD_EN
field.description: RTC 1 kHz timer wake-up enable for Deep power-down.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disable. A match on the 1 kHz RTC timer will not bring the part out of Deep power-down mode.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. A match on the 1 kHz RTC timer bring the part out of Deep power-down mode.

field.name: RTC1KHZ_EN
field.description: RTC 1 kHz clock enable. This bit can be set to 0 to conserve power if the 1 kHz timer is not used. This bit has no effect when the RTC is disabled (bit 7 of this register is 0).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disable. A match on the 1 kHz RTC timer will not bring the part out of Deep power-down mode.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. The 1 kHz RTC timer is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disable. The RTC 1 Hz and 1 kHz clocks are shut down and the RTC operation is disabled. This bit should be 0 when writing to load a value in the RTC counter register.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. The 1 Hz RTC clock is running and RTC operation is enabled. This bit must be set to initiate operation of the RTC. The first clock to the RTC counter occurs 1 s after this bit is set. To also enable the high-resolution, 1 kHz clock, set bit 6 in this register.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: The RTC oscillator is enabled. This bit must be cleared in order for the RTC module to function

enumeratedValue.name: SHUT_OFF
enumeratedValue.description: The RTC oscillator is shut-off to reserve power consumption. RTC operation is disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: The sub-second counter (if implemented) is disabled. This bit is cleared by a system-level POR or BOD reset as well as a by the RTC_ENA bit (bit 7 in this register). On modules not equipped with a sub-second counter, this bit will always read-back as a '0'

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: The 32 KHz sub-second counter is enabled (if implemented). Counting will commence on the start of the first one-second interval after this bit is set. Note: This bit can only be set after the RTC_ENA bit (bit 7) has been set by a previous write operation. Note: The RTC sub-second counter must be re-enabled whenever the chip exits deep_powerdown mode.

field.name: MATVAL
field.description: Contains the match value against which the 1 Hz RTC timer will be compared to set the alarm flag RTC_ALARM and generate an alarm interrupt/wake-up if enabled.

field.name: VAL
field.description: A read reflects the current value of the main, 1 Hz RTC timer. A write loads a new initial value into the timer. The RTC counter will count up continuously at a 1 Hz rate once the RTC Software Reset is removed (by clearing bit 0 of the CTRL register). Only write to this register when the RTC_EN bit in the RTC CTRL Register is 0. The counter increments one second after the RTC_EN bit is set.

field.name: VAL
field.description: A read reflects the current value of the high-resolution/wake-up timer. A write pre-loads a start count value into the wake-up timer and initializes a count-down sequence. Do not write to this register while counting is in progress.

field.name: RTC_SUBSEC
field.description: A read reflects the current value of the 32Khz sub-second counter. This counter will be cleared whenever the SUBSEC_ENA bit in the RTC_CONTROL register is low. Up-counting at a 32 KHz rate commences at the start of the next one-second interval after the SUBSEC_ENA bit is set. This counter must be re-enabled after exiting deep_powerdown mode or after the main RTC module has been disabled and re-enabled. On modules not equipped with a sub-second counter, this register will read-back as all zeroes.

field.name: GPDATA
field.description: Data retained during Deep power-down mode or loss of main power as long as VBAT is supplied.

enumeratedValue.name: invw0
enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, invalidate all lines in way 0.

enumeratedValue.name: pushw0
enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, push all modified lines in way 0

enumeratedValue.name: invw1
enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, invalidate all lines in way 1

enumeratedValue.name: pushw1
enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, push all modified lines in way 1

enumeratedValue.name: no_effect
enumeratedValue.description: Write: no effect. Read: no cache command active.

enumeratedValue.name: init_cmd
enumeratedValue.description: Write: initiate command indicated by bits 27-24. Read: cache command active.

enumeratedValue.name: no_effect
enumeratedValue.description: Write: no effect. Read: no line command active.

enumeratedValue.name: init_cmd
enumeratedValue.description: Write: initiate line command indicated by bits 27-24. Read: line command active.

enumeratedValue.name: no_effect
enumeratedValue.description: Write: no effect. Read: no line command active.

enumeratedValue.name: init_cmd
enumeratedValue.description: Write: initiate line command indicated by bits CLCR[27:24]. Read: line command active.

enumeratedValue.name: MASTER_OFF
enumeratedValue.description: MASTER_OFF: Master is off (is not enabled). If MASTER_OFF is enabled, then the I3C module can only use slave mode.

enumeratedValue.name: MASTER_ON
enumeratedValue.description: MASTER_ON: Master is on (is enabled). When used from start-up, this I3C module is master by default (the main master). The module will control the bus unless the master is handed off. If the master is handed off, then MSTENA must move to 2 after that happens. The handoff means emitting GETACCMST and if accepted, the module will emit a STOP and set the MSTENA bit to 2 (or 0).

enumeratedValue.name: MASTER_CAPABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MASTER_CAPABLE: The I3C module is master-capable; however the module is operating as a slave now. When used from the start, the I3C module will start as a slave, but will be prepared to switch to master mode. To switch to master mode, the slave emits an Master Request (MR), or gets a GETACCMST CCC command and accepts it (to switch on the STOP).

enumeratedValue.name: NONE
enumeratedValue.description: NONE: Use PUR (Pull-Up Resistor). Hold SCL High.

enumeratedValue.name: WIRED_IN
enumeratedValue.description: WIRED_IN: Wired-in High Keeper controls; use pin_HK (High Keeper) controls.

enumeratedValue.name: PASSIVE_SDA
enumeratedValue.description: PASSIVE_SDA: Passive on SDA; can Hi-Z (high impedance) for Bus Free (IDLE) and hold.

enumeratedValue.name: PASSIVE_ON_SDA_SCL
enumeratedValue.description: PASSIVE_ON_SDA_SCL: Passive on SDA and SCL; can Hi-Z (high impedance) both for Bus Free (IDLE), and can Hi-Z SDA for hold.

enumeratedValue.name: NONE
enumeratedValue.description: NONE: no event or no pending event

enumeratedValue.name: NO_REQUEST
enumeratedValue.description: NO_REQUEST: Request not sent yet. Either there was no START yet, or is waiting for Bus-Available or Bus-Idle (HJ).

enumeratedValue.name: NACKED
enumeratedValue.description: NACKED: Not acknowledged(Request sent and NACKed); the module will try again.

enumeratedValue.name: ACKED
enumeratedValue.description: ACKED: Acknowledged (Request sent and ACKed), so Done (unless the time control data is still being sent).

field.name: ACTSTATE
field.description: Activity state from Common Command Codes (CCC)

enumeratedValue.name: NO_TIME_CONTROL
enumeratedValue.description: NO_TIME_CONTROL: No time control is enabled

enumeratedValue.name: ASYNC_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: ASYNC_MODE: Asynchronous standard mode (0) is enabled

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: NORMAL_MODE: If EVENT is set to 0 after was a non-0 value, event processing will cancel if the event processing has not yet started; if event processing has already been started, then event processing will not be be cancelled.

enumeratedValue.name: IBI
enumeratedValue.description: IBI: Start an In-Band Interrupt. This will try to push an IBI interrupt onto the I3C bus. If data is associated with the IBI, then the data will be read from the SCTRL.IBIDATA field. If time control is enabled, then this data will also include any time control-related bytes; additionally, the IBIDATA byte will have bit 7 set to 1 automatically (as is required for time control). The IBI interrupt will occur after the 1st (mandatory) IBIDATA, if any.

enumeratedValue.name: HOT_JOIN_REQUEST
enumeratedValue.description: HOT_JOIN_REQUEST: Start a Hot-Join request. A Hot-Join Request should only be used when the device is powered on after the I3C bus is already powered up, or when the device is connected using hot insertion methods (the device is powered up when it is physically inserted onto the powered-up I3C bus). The hot join will wait for Bus Idle, and SCTRL.EVENT=HOT_JOIN_REQUEST must be set before the slave enable (SCONFIG.SLVENA).

field.name: CCC
field.description: Common Command Code (CCC) (that was not handled by I3C module) interrupt enable

field.name: CHANDLED
field.description: Common Command Code (CCC) (that was handled by I3C module) interrupt enable

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE_ONE_FRAME
enumeratedValue.description: ENABLE_ONE_FRAME: DMA is enabled for 1 Frame (ended by DMA or terminated). DMATB auto-clears on a STOP or START (see the Match START or STOP bit (SCONFIG.MATCHSS).

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: ENABLE: DMA is enabled until turned off. Normally, ENABLE should only be used with Master Message mode.

enumeratedValue.name: HALF_WORD
enumeratedValue.description: HALF_WORD: Half word (16 bits). This will make sure that 2 bytes are free/available in the FIFO.

field.name: TXTRIG
field.description: Trigger level for TX FIFO emptiness

enumeratedValue.name: TRIGGRONELESS
enumeratedValue.description: Trigger on 1 less than full or less (Default)

field.name: RXTRIG
field.description: Trigger level for RX FIFO fullness

field.name: DATA
field.description: The data byte to send to the master

field.name: DATA
field.description: The data byte to send to the master

field.name: DATA0
field.description: The 1st byte to send to the master

field.name: DATA1
field.description: The 2nd byte to send to the master

register.name: SWDATAHE
register.description: Slave Write Data Half-word End Register

field.name: DATA0
field.description: The 1st byte to send to the master

field.name: DATA1
field.description: The 2nd byte to send to the master

field.name: LSB
field.description: The 1st byte read from the slave

field.name: MSB
field.description: The 2nd byte read from the slave

enumeratedValue.name: HW_BUT
enumeratedValue.description: HW_BUT: in hardware but the I3C module instance handles ID 48b.

enumeratedValue.name: PARTNO
enumeratedValue.description: PARTNO: a part number register (PARTNO) handles ID 48b

enumeratedValue.name: MASTERNOTSUPPORTED
enumeratedValue.description: MASTERNOTSUPPORTED: master capability is not supported.

enumeratedValue.name: STATIC
enumeratedValue.description: STATIC: Static address is fixed in hardware

enumeratedValue.name: HW_CONTROL
enumeratedValue.description: HW_CONTROL: Hardware controls the static address dynamically (for example, from the pin strap)

enumeratedValue.name: CONFIG
enumeratedValue.description: CONFIG: SCONFIG register supplies the static address

field.name: IBI_MR_HJ
field.description: In-Band Interrupts, Master Requests, Hot Join events

enumeratedValue.name: NO_TIME_CONTROL_TYPE
enumeratedValue.description: NO_TIME_CONTROL_TYPE: No time control is enabled

enumeratedValue.name: ATLEAST1_TIME_CONTROL
enumeratedValue.description: ATLEAST1_TIME_CONTROL: at least one time-control type is supported

enumeratedValue.name: FIFO_2BYTE
enumeratedValue.description: FIFO_2BYTE: 2-byte TX FIFO, the default FIFO transmit value (FIFOTX)

enumeratedValue.name: FIFO_2BYTE
enumeratedValue.description: FIFO_2BYTE: 2 (or 3)-byte RX FIFO, the default FIFO receive value (FIFORX)

enumeratedValue.name: DANOTASSIGNED
enumeratedValue.description: DANOTASSIGNED: a Dynamic Address is not assigned

enumeratedValue.name: DAASSIGNED
enumeratedValue.description: DAASSIGNED: a Dynamic Address is assigned

enumeratedValue.name: NONE
enumeratedValue.description: NONE: Returns to this when finished with any request. The MSTATUS register indicates the master's state. See also AutoIBI mode. NONE is only written as 0: when setting RDTERM to 1 (to stop a read in progress) or when setting IBI reponse field (IBIRESP) for MSG use

enumeratedValue.name: EMITSTARTADDR
enumeratedValue.description: EMITSTARTADDR: Emit START with address and direction from a stopped state or in the middle of a Single Data Rate (SDR) message. If from a stopped state (IDLE), then emit start may be prevented by an event (like IBI, MR, HJ), in which case the appropriate interrupt is signaled; note that Emit START can be resubmitted.

enumeratedValue.name: EMITSTOP
enumeratedValue.description: EMITSTOP: Emit a STOP on bus. Must be in Single Data Rate (SDR) mode. If in Dynamic Address Assignment (DAA) mode, Emit stop will exit DAA mode.

enumeratedValue.name: IBIACKNACK
enumeratedValue.description: IBIACKNACK: Manual In-Band Interrupt (IBI) Acknowledge (ACK) or Not Acknowledge (NACK). When IBIRESP has indicated a hold on an In-Band Interrupt to allow a manual decision, this request completes it. Uses IBIRESP to provide the information.

enumeratedValue.name: PROCESSDAA
enumeratedValue.description: PROCESSDAA: If not in Dynamic Address Assignment (DAA) mode now, will issue START, 7E, ENTDAA, and then will emit 7E/R to process each slave. Will stop just before the new Dynamic Address (DA) is to be emitted. The next Process DAA request will use the Addr field as the new DA to assign. If NACKed on the 7E/R, then the interrupt will indicate this situation, and a STOP will be emitted.

enumeratedValue.name: FORCEEXIT
enumeratedValue.description: FORCEEXIT and IBHR: Emit an Exit Pattern from any state, but end Double Data Rate (DDR) (including MSGDDR), if in DDR mode now. Includes a STOP afterward. If TYPE != 0, then it will perform an IBHR (In-Band Hardware Reset). If TYPE=2, then it does a normal reset (DEFRST can prevent the reset). If TYPE=3, it does a forced reset (will always reset).

enumeratedValue.name: AUTOIBI
enumeratedValue.description: AUTOIBI: Hold in a stopped state, but auto-emit START,7E when the slave is holding down SDA to get an In-Band Interrupt (IBI). Actual In-Band Interrupt handling is defined by IBIRESP.

enumeratedValue.name: I3C
enumeratedValue.description: I3C: Normally the SDR mode of I3C. For ForceExit, the Exit pattern.

enumeratedValue.name: I2C
enumeratedValue.description: I2C: Normally the Standard I2C protocol.

enumeratedValue.name: DDR
enumeratedValue.description: DDR: (Double Data Rate): Normally the HDR-DDR mode of I3C. Enter DDR mode (7E and then ENTHDR0), if the module is not already in DDR mode. The 1st byte written to the TX FIFO should be a command, and should already be in the FIFO. To end DDR mode, use ForceExit. For ForceExit, the normal IBHR (In-Band Hardware Reset).

enumeratedValue.name: FORCEDIBHR
enumeratedValue.description: For ForcedExit, this is forced IBHR.

enumeratedValue.name: ACK
enumeratedValue.description: ACK: Acknowledge. A mandatory byte (or not) is decided by the Master In-band Interrupt Registry and Rules Register (MIBIRULES). To limit the maximum number of IBI bytes, configure the Read Termination field (MCTRL.RDTERM).

enumeratedValue.name: ACK_WITH_MANDATORY
enumeratedValue.description: ACK_WITH_MANDATORY: Acknowledge with mandatory byte (ignores the MIBIRULES register). Acknowledge with mandatory byte should not be used, unless only slaves with a mandatory byte can cause an In-Band Interrupt.

enumeratedValue.name: MANUAL
enumeratedValue.description: MANUAL: stop and wait for a decision using the IBIAckNack request

enumeratedValue.name: SLVREQ
enumeratedValue.description: SLVREQ: (Slave Request state) the bus has STOPped but a slave is holding SDA low. If using auto-emit IBI (MCTRL.AutoIBI), then the master will not stay in the Slave Request state.

enumeratedValue.name: MSGSDR
enumeratedValue.description: MSGSDR: in Single Data Rate (SDR) Message state (from using MWMSG_SDR)

enumeratedValue.name: NORMACT
enumeratedValue.description: NORMACT: normal active Single Data Rate (SDR) state (from using MCTRL and MWDATAn and MRDATAn registers). The master will stay in the NORMACT state until a STOP is issued.

enumeratedValue.name: DDR
enumeratedValue.description: MSGDDR: in Double Data Rate (DDR) Message mode (from using MWMSG_DDR or using the normal method with DDR). The master will stay in the DDR state, until the master exits using EXIT (emits the Exit pattern).

enumeratedValue.name: DAA
enumeratedValue.description: DAA: in Enter Dynamic Address Assignment (ENTDAA) mode

enumeratedValue.name: IBIACK
enumeratedValue.description: IBIACK: waiting for an In-Band Interrupt (IBI) ACK/NACK decision

enumeratedValue.name: IBIRCV
enumeratedValue.description: IBIRCV: Receiving an In-Band Interrupt (IBI); this IBIRCV state is used after IBI/MR/HJ has won the arbitration, and IBIRCV state is also used for IBI mandatory byte (if any) and any bytes that follow.

field.name: BETWEEN
field.description: Between messages or Dynamic Address Assignments (DAA)

enumeratedValue.name: NONE
enumeratedValue.description: NONE: cleared when IBI Won bit (MSTATUS.IBIWON) is cleared

field.name: NOWMASTER
field.description: Now master (now this I3C module is a master) interrupt enable

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE_ONE_FRAME
enumeratedValue.description: ENABLE_ONE_FRAME: DMA is enabled for 1 frame. DMAFB auto-clears on STOP or repeated START. See MCONFIG.MATCHSS.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: ENABLE: DMA is enabled until the DMA is turned off.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE_ONE_FRAME
enumeratedValue.description: ENABLE_ONE_FRAME: DMA is enabled for 1 frame (ended by DMA or Terminated). DMATB auto-clears on STOP or START. See MCONFIG.MATCHSS.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: ENABLE: DMA is enabled until DMA is turned off. Normally DMA ENABLE should only be used in Master Message mode.

enumeratedValue.name: HALF_WORD
enumeratedValue.description: HALF_WORD: Half-word (16 bits). This will make sure that 2 bytes are free/available in FIFO.

field.name: DMA1EN
field.description: Enables the DMA use on the 1st channel for eSPI and selects what triggers it

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. The DMA channel is not used

enumeratedValue.name: TRIGGERD_ON_HOST_READ
enumeratedValue.description: Triggers on Host Read empty (whether endpoint and a byte or mailbox and many bytes). Allows reload of memory

enumeratedValue.name: TRIGGERS_ON_HOST_WRITE
enumeratedValue.description: Triggers on Host Write complete/ready (whether endpoint and a byte or mailbox and many bytes).

field.name: DMA0PORT
field.description: Selects which port is operating the DMA: Value Meaning 0 to 7 Is normal port number up to max ports (e

field.name: DMA1PORT
field.description: Selects which port is operating the DMA: Value Meaning 0 to 7 Is normal port number up to max ports (e

field.name: CNT0
field.description: Used with Mailbox and Bus master to allow RAM contents to be copied

field.name: CNT1
field.description: Used with Mailbox and Bus master to allow RAM contents to be copied

register.name: RAMBASE
register.description: Address of RAM to use for data. This tells the application where the RAM is located (up to 16K addressable).

field.name: RAM
field.description: Is location in System memory space where RAM is located that is used by this peripheral's bus master

register.name: MAPBASE
register.description: Base0 and Base1 mapped offsets for ports

register.name: IRQPUSH
register.description: IRQ to drive into Host (with eSPI)

field.name: IRQ
field.description: Set to the IRQ to push across to the Host.

field.name: DONE
field.description: Will go to 1 when complete; this is just the same bit as IrqUpd in MSTAT, which can interrupt using INTENSET

register.name: WIREWO
register.description: Wire states for Host to see; if LPC, this is the IRQ states.

field.name: DONE
field.description: Set to 1 after last write has been pushed out to Host

field.name: WIRES
field.description: eSPI: Indicates the latest states from the Host via VWire

field.name: CNT
field.description: A counter (set to 0 on enable of p80) which increments with each new value. Will wrap back to 0.

register.name: STATADDR
register.description: Location of Status block in memory space, if enabled.

field.name: OFF
field.description: The offset in Host space for the status block. It must be double-word aligned.

field.name: BASE
field.description: The meaning is dependent on type of port:

enumeratedValue.name: OFFSET
enumeratedValue.description: Is offset from 0 in host memory or IO space.

enumeratedValue.name: BASE1
enumeratedValue.description: Uses Base1 offset in host memory (see MAPBASE reg)

enumeratedValue.name: BASE2
enumeratedValue.description: Uses Base2 offset in host memory (see MAPBASE reg)

register.name: ESPICAP
register.description: eSPI Capabilities of MCU to send to Host

field.name: SPICAP
field.description: SPI mode allowed (host still has to select):

field.name: MAXSPD
field.description: Maximum SPI Clock speed to allow (host still chooses):

field.name: ALPIN
field.description: Allow Alert to be a pin if the Host wants

field.name: MEMMX
field.description: If 1, allow 128 byte payload for memory and OOB access, else limit to 64

field.name: FLASHMX
field.description: Selects max Flash payload size to allow:

field.name: SAF
field.description: If 1, then Slave Attached Flash is possible with this firmware

field.name: SAFERA
field.description: Min Erase sector size allowed if SAF used

field.name: MEMSZ
field.description: If 1, will use 128 byte payload for memory and OOB access, else limited to 64

field.name: FLASHSZ
field.description: Indicates max Flash payload size selected using same values as FLASHMX

field.name: ALERT
field.description: Alert is a pin vs. MISO

field.name: ALERTOD
field.description: Alert is OD as a pin

field.name: SPISPD
field.description: SPI Speed selected by Host. See note in section 2.2 on higher eSPI clock speeds and system setup.

field.name: SAF
field.description: Is 1 if Slave Attached Flash is enabled. Only possible if SAF is set in ESPICAP.

register.name: ESPIMISC
register.description: Miscellaneous uses, such as Alert pin as GPIO (when not used for Alert).

field.name: GPIO_OE
field.description: Set to 1 to make the Alert/Reset pin an output GPIO, else is input (High-Z)

field.name: GPIO_OD
field.description: Set to 1 to make the Alert/Reset pin act open-drain when GPIO_OE=1

field.name: GPIO_IN
field.description: Is the current state of the Alert/Reset pin, whether in input mode or not

field.name: PWRSAV
field.description: This bit, when set, will employ clock gating for the eSPI side

field.name: Type
field.description: The Type field selects how the port interacts with the Host over the eSPI or LPC bus

field.name: Direction
field.description: Meaning depends on Type, but generally picks the direction of the port (Host writes, Host reads, or both)

field.name: MBIntAll
field.description: Mailbox: Map interrupt on Read 1st and Write 1st to every read/write (special will still control 0th and last location)

field.name: StallRd
field.description: Stall on any Read of Index/Data and Mailbox (only)

field.name: StallWr
field.description: Stall on any Write of Index/Data and Mailbox

field.name: ErrorIgn
field.description: If 1, the Host will get an error when trying to perform a read or write that is blocked by the Direction field

field.name: INTRD
field.description: Interrupt was caused by Read or 1st Read or Bus master Started.

field.name: INTWR
field.description: Interrupt was caused by Write or 1st Write or Bus master Started.

field.name: INTSPC
field.description: Interrupt was caused by: Bit Endpoint Idx/Data Mbox BusMaster/Flash SPC0 CMD Idx Change Write 0 Completed SPC1 - - Read 0 - SPC2 - - Write Last - SPC3 - - Read Last -

field.name: ERR
field.description: Cause of INTERR: Bit Endpoint, Idx/Data Mbox BusMaster/Flash ERR0 Host Write Over Host Write or Read invalid for Access Failed From-Host (cannot tell on Memory To-Host, but can for Flash write)

register.name: P0IRuleStat
register.description: The Port Set Interrupt-Rule and Set User Status register is used to set: The interrupt causes per port. That is, it is used to select what events from the port should cause an interrupt, if any. The user Status bits. The status byte returned to the host will be composed of both these user bits (which the application defines) and automatically generated status. The interrupt masks then are matched by sticky cause bits in PnSTAT (which can be read and then write-1 cleared). The sticky bits are set whether the interrupt is masked or not, but the masks cause an interrupt when the bits are set and the port is int enabled via INTENSET.

field.name: USTAT
field.description: User defined status bits. These are salted into the status register as specified in section 4.1 and 4.6.

field.name: INTERR
field.description: Interrupt if an error is detected (classes of error defined in section 2.14)

field.name: INTRD
field.description: Interrupt if Read or 1st Read or Bus master Started.

field.name: INTWR
field.description: Interrupt if Write or 1st Write or Bus master Finished.

field.name: INTSPC
field.description: Interrupt if: Bit Endpoint Idx/Data Mbox BusMaster/Flash SPC0 CMD Idx Change Write 0 Completed SPC1 - - Read 0 - SPC2 - - Write Last - SPC3 - - Read Last -

field.name: SRST
field.description: Resets the RdStatus and WrStatus in PStatus register

register.name: P0ADDR
register.description: The Port Address register is used to set the mapped address in the LPC/eSPI memory space. For normal Ports, this is a 16-bit location in IO space or a 32-bit offset into PCIe address mapped space. It is not used for OOB, Bus Mastering, or Flash; see the PnOMFLEN register for those. For Endpoints, it is the base of a dword (64 bits). For Index/Data, it is the base of a word (32 bits). For mailbox memory, the address is modulus the length of the mailbox (x2 for both directions). So, if a 16-byte mailbox (single), the offset must have bits 3:0 set to 0 (that is &~0xF). If split directions, then normally bits 4:0 would be set to 0 (that is &~0x1F).

field.name: OFF
field.description: Offset from 0 or the selected mapped base for matching memory or IO

field.name: BASE_or_ASZ
field.description: The meaning is dependent on type of port:

enumeratedValue.name: OFFSET_FROM_0
enumeratedValue.description: Is offset from 0 in host memory or IO space.

enumeratedValue.name: USE_BASE0
enumeratedValue.description: Uses BASE0 offset in host memory

enumeratedValue.name: USE_BASE1
enumeratedValue.description: Uses BASE1 offset in host memory

field.name: IDXOFF
field.description: For index/register only: This is the byte offset of the Index relative to the data (before or after, based on IDX1ST)

field.name: IDX1ST
field.description: For index/data register only: Is 1 if index is lower address than data (e

register.name: P0OMFLEN
register.description: The Port OOB, Mastering, Flash length is used for OOB to Host and Bus Mastering and Flash to or from Host. The PnADDR register is not used for either OOB or Bus Mastering. Instead, this register (in same location) is written with byte length message (including address for Mastering and Flash) along with direction. Writing to the SSTCL field of the PIRuleState will notify the Host to perform the transaction. Clearing it before the Host has started a transaction will cancel it, but only if it has not yet seen the Status.

field.name: LEN
field.description: Length in bytes, 0 relative, to Send for OOB, Send or Retrieve for Mastering, Read or Write for Flash, Erase (in blocks) for Flash, or read data for SAF read

field.name: TRANS
field.description: Transfer request as: Type Value Meaning OOB 0 To Host OOB 1, 2, 3 Not used Master 0 To Host 32 (Host reads w/32-bit address) Master 1 To Host 64 (Host reads w/64-bit address) Master 2 From Host 32 (Host writes w/32-bit address) Master 3 From Host 64 (Host writes w/64-bit address) MAF Flash 1 Read Flash (location in RAM) MAF Flash 2 Write Flash (location in RAM) MAF Flash 3 Erase Flash (sector in RAM) SAF 0 Completion fail SAF 1 Completion with data SAF 2 Completion with no data

field.name: DATA_LEN
field.description: Meaning is dependent on type of port: If endpoint or index/data: is data byte If Mailbox or Bus master or Flash: is count in last message, 0 relative If SAF, is count in last message including address (so, +4), 0 relative

field.name: DIR
field.description: Direction of last access: 0 = Read By Host 1 = Write By Host

field.name: DATA
field.description: Data to send to Host. Application can tell when taken via the PnStatus register.

field.name: OFF
field.description: This is the word offset into the RAM

field.name: LEN
field.description: This is the length of the mailbox or mastering area as 4<<LEN per direction

register.name: P4IRuleStat
register.description: The Port Set Interrupt-Rule and Set User Status register is used to set: The interrupt causes per port. That is, it is used to select what events from the port should cause an interrupt, if any. The user Status bits. The status byte returned to the host will be composed of both these user bits (which the application defines) and automatically generated status. The interrupt masks then are matched by sticky cause bits in PnSTAT (which can be read and then write-1 cleared). The sticky bits are set whether the interrupt is masked or not, but the masks cause an interrupt when the bits are set and the port is int enabled via INTENSET.

register.name: P4ADDR
register.description: The Port Address register is used to set the mapped address in the LPC/eSPI memory space. For normal Ports, this is a 16-bit location in IO space or a 32-bit offset into PCIe address mapped space. It is not used for OOB, Bus Mastering, or Flash; see the PnOMFLEN register for those. For Endpoints, it is the base of a dword (64 bits). For Index/Data, it is the base of a word (32 bits). For mailbox memory, the address is modulus the length of the mailbox (x2 for both directions). So, if a 16-byte mailbox (single), the offset must have bits 3:0 set to 0 (that is &~0xF). If split directions, then normally bits 4:0 would be set to 0 (that is &~0x1F).

Instead, this register (in same location) is written with byte length message (including address for Mastering and Flash) along with direction. Writing to the SSTCL field of the PIRuleState will notify the Host to perform the transaction. register.name: B_[%s]
register.description: Byte pin registers for all port 0 and 1 GPIO pins

field.name: PBYTE
field.description: Read: state of the pin PIOm_n, regardless of direction, masking, or alternate function, except that pins configured as analog I/O always read as 0. One register for each port pin. Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. Write: loads the pin's output bit. One register for each port pin. Supported pins depends on the specific device and package.

register.name: W_[%s]
register.description: Word pin registers for all port 0 and 1 GPIO pins

field.name: PWORD
field.description: Read 0: pin PIOm_n is LOW. Write 0: clear output bit. Read 0xFFFF FFFF: pin PIOm_n is HIGH. Write any value 0x0000 0001 to 0xFFFF FFFF: set output bit. Only 0 or 0xFFFF FFFF can be read. Writing any value other than 0 will set the output bit. One register for each port pin. Supported pins depends on the specific device and package.

field.name: DIRP
field.description: Selects pin direction for pin PIOm_n (bit 0 = PIOn_0, bit 1 = PIOn_1, etc.). Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. 0 = input. 1 = output.

field.name: MASKP
field.description: Controls which bits corresponding to PIOm_n are active in the MPORT register (bit 0 = PIOn_0, bit 1 = PIOn_1, etc.). Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. 0 = Read MPORT: pin state; write MPORT: load output bit. 1 = Read MPORT: 0; write MPORT: output bit not affected.

field.name: PORT
field.description: Reads pin states or loads output bits (bit 0 = PIOn_0, bit 1 = PIOn_1, etc.). Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. 0 = Read: pin is low; write: clear output bit. 1 = Read: pin is high; write: set output bit.

field.name: MPORTP
field.description: Masked port register (bit 0 = PIOn_0, bit 1 = PIOn_1, etc.). Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. 0 = Read: pin is LOW and/or the corresponding bit in the MASK register is 1; write: clear output bit if the corresponding bit in the MASK register is 0. 1 = Read: pin is HIGH and the corresponding bit in the MASK register is 0; write: set output bit if the corresponding bit in the MASK register is 0.

register.name: SET[%s]
register.description: Write: Set register for port Read: output bits for port

field.name: SETP
field.description: Read or set output bits (bit 0 = PIOn_0, bit 1 = PIOn_1, etc.). Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. 0 = Read: output bit: write: no operation. 1 = Read: output bit; write: set output bit.

field.name: CLRP
field.description: Clear output bits (bit 0 = PIOn_0, bit 1 = PIOn_1, etc.). Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. 0 = No operation. 1 = Clear output bit.

field.name: NOTP
field.description: Toggle output bits (bit 0 = PIOn_0, bit 1 = PIOn_1, etc.). Supported pins depends on the specific device and package. 0 = no operation. 1 = Toggle output bit.

cluster.name: CHANNEL[%s]
cluster.description: Array of registers: CFG, CTLSTAT, XFERCFG

field.name: PERIPHREQEN
field.description: Peripheral request Enable. If a DMA channel is used to perform a memory-to-memory move, any peripheral DMA request associated with that channel can be disabled to prevent any interaction between the peripheral and the DMA controller.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. Peripheral DMA requests are disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. Peripheral DMA requests are enabled.

field.name: HWTRIGEN
field.description: Hardware Triggering Enable for this channel.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. Hardware triggering is not used.

field.name: TRIGPOL
field.description: Trigger Polarity. Selects the polarity of a hardware trigger for this channel.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING
enumeratedValue.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING
enumeratedValue.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.

field.name: TRIGTYPE
field.description: Trigger Type. Selects hardware trigger as edge triggered or level triggered.

enumeratedValue.name: EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.

enumeratedValue.name: LEVEL
enumeratedValue.description: Level. Hardware trigger is level triggered. Note that when level triggering without burst (BURSTPOWER = 0) is selected, only hardware triggers should be used on that channel. Transfers continue as long as the trigger level is asserted. Once the trigger is de-asserted, the transfer will be paused until the trigger is, again, asserted. However, the transfer will not be paused until any remaining transfers within the current BURSTPOWER length are completed.

field.name: TRIGBURST
field.description: Trigger Burst. Selects whether hardware triggers cause a single or burst transfer.

enumeratedValue.name: SINGLE
enumeratedValue.description: Single transfer. Hardware trigger causes a single transfer.

enumeratedValue.name: BURST
enumeratedValue.description: Burst transfer. When the trigger for this channel is set to edge triggered, a hardware trigger causes a burst transfer, as defined by BURSTPOWER. When the trigger for this channel is set to level triggered, a hardware trigger causes transfers to continue as long as the trigger is asserted, unless the transfer is complete.

field.name: BURSTPOWER
field.description: Burst Power is used in two ways. It always selects the address wrap size when SRCBURSTWRAP and/or DSTBURSTWRAP modes are selected (see descriptions elsewhere in this register).
