register.name: USB1_VBUS_DETECT
register.description: USB PHY VBUS Detect Control Register

field.name: VBUSVALID_THRESH
field.description: Sets the threshold for the VBUSVALID comparator

enumeratedValue.name: VBUS_OVERRIDE_EN_0
enumeratedValue.description: Use the results of the internal VBUS_VALID and Session Valid comparators for VBUS_VALID, AVALID, BVALID, and SESSEND (Default)

enumeratedValue.name: VBUS_OVERRIDE_EN_1
enumeratedValue.description: Use the override values for VBUS_VALID, AVALID, BVALID, and SESSEND

field.name: SESSEND_OVERRIDE
field.description: Override value for SESSEND The bit field provides the value for USB1_VBUS_DET_STAT[0] if USB_VBUS_DETECT[3] is set to value 1'b1

field.name: BVALID_OVERRIDE
field.description: Override value for B-Device Session Valid The bit field provides the value for USB1_VBUS_DET_STAT[1] if USB_VBUS_DETECT[3] is set to value 1'b1

field.name: AVALID_OVERRIDE
field.description: Override value for A-Device Session Valid The bit field provides the value for USB1_VBUS_DET_STAT[2] if USB_VBUS_DETECT[3] is set to value 1'b1

field.name: VBUSVALID_OVERRIDE
field.description: Override value for VBUS_VALID signal sent to USB controller The bit field provides the value for VBUS_VALID reported to the USB controller if the value of USB1_VBUS_DETECT[3] is set to 1'b1

field.name: VBUSVALID_SEL
field.description: Selects the source of the VBUS_VALID signal reported to the USB controller This is one of the bit fields that selects the source of the VBUS_VALID signal reported to the USB controller

enumeratedValue.name: VBUSVALID_SEL_0
enumeratedValue.description: Use the VBUS_VALID comparator results for signal reported to the USB controller (Default)

enumeratedValue.name: VBUSVALID_SEL_1
enumeratedValue.description: Use the VBUS_VALID_3V detector results for signal reported to the USB controller

field.name: VBUS_SOURCE_SEL
field.description: Selects the source of the VBUS_VALID signal reported to the USB controller This is one of the bit fields that selects the source of the VBUS_VALID signal reported to the USB controller

enumeratedValue.name: VBUS_SOURCE_SEL_0
enumeratedValue.description: Use the VBUS_VALID comparator results for signal reported to the USB controller (Default)

enumeratedValue.name: VBUS_SOURCE_SEL_1
enumeratedValue.description: Use the Session Valid comparator results for signal reported to the USB controller

enumeratedValue.name: VBUS_SOURCE_SEL_2
enumeratedValue.description: Use the Session Valid comparator results for signal reported to the USB controller

field.name: VBUSVALID_TO_SESSVALID
field.description: Selects the comparator used for VBUS_VALID This bit field controls the comparator used to report the VBUS_VALID results in USB1_VBUS_DETECT[3] between the VBUS_VALID comparator and the Session Valid comparator

enumeratedValue.name: VBUSVALID_TO_SESSVALID_0
enumeratedValue.description: Use the VBUS_VALID comparator for VBUS_VALID results

enumeratedValue.name: VBUSVALID_TO_SESSVALID_1
enumeratedValue.description: Use the Session End comparator for VBUS_VALID results. The Session End threshold is >0.8V and <4.0V.

field.name: PWRUP_CMPS
field.description: Enables the VBUS_VALID comparator Powers up the comparator used for the VBUS_VALID detector

field.name: DISCHARGE_VBUS
field.description: Controls VBUS discharge resistor This bit field controls a nominal 22kohm resistor between the USB1_VBUS pin and ground

field.name: EN_CHARGER_RESISTOR
field.description: Enables resistors used for an older method of resistive battery charger detection

enumeratedValue.name: EN_CHARGER_RESISTOR_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disable resistive charger detection resistors on USB_DP and USB_DP

enumeratedValue.name: EN_CHARGER_RESISTOR_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enable resistive charger detection resistors on USB_DP and USB_DP

enumeratedValue.name: NO_START
enumeratedValue.description: Do not start the sequence. Writes of this value have no effect.

enumeratedValue.name: START
enumeratedValue.description: Initiate the charger detection sequence. If the sequence is already running, writes of this value have no effect.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Do not perform a software reset.

field.name: CLOCK_UNIT
field.description: Unit of Measurement Encoding for Clock Speed

field.name: CLOCK_SPEED
field.description: Numerical Value of Clock Speed in Binary

enumeratedValue.name: CONN_SDP
enumeratedValue.description: Attached to an SDP. Must comply with USB 2.0 by drawing only 2.5 mA (max) until connected.

enumeratedValue.name: CONN_CP
enumeratedValue.description: Attached to a charging port. The exact meaning depends on bit 18 (value 0: Attached to either a CDP or a DCP. The charger type detection has not completed. value 1: Attached to a CDP. The charger type detection has completed.)

enumeratedValue.name: NO_DATA_PIN_CONN
enumeratedValue.description: The module is either not enabled, or the module is enabled but the data pins have not yet been detected.

enumeratedValue.name: DATA_PIN_CONN
enumeratedValue.description: Data pin contact detection is complete.

enumeratedValue.name: SEQ_ERR
enumeratedValue.description: Error in the detection sequence. See the SEQ_STAT field to determine the phase in which the error occurred.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: The detection sequence has not been running for over 1 s.

enumeratedValue.name: TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: It has been over 1 s since the data pin contact was detected and debounced.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_OVERRIDE
enumeratedValue.description: No overrides. Bit field must remain at this value during normal USB data communication to prevent unexpected conditions on USB_DP and USB_DM pins. (Default)

enumeratedValue.name: PRI_DET_OVERRIDE
enumeratedValue.description: Enables VDP_SRC voltage source for the USB_DP pin and IDM_SINK current source for the USB_DM pin.

field.name: TDCD_DBNC

field.name: VBUS_DEBOUNCED
field.description: This bit indicates if VBUS is detected or not.

field.name: PHY_TEST_MODE

field.name: ERR_CODE

field.name: SKIP

field.name: EP_INT_EN
field.description: If this bit is set and the corresponding USB interrupt status bit is set, a HW interrupt is generated on the interrupt line.

field.name: FRAME_INT_EN
field.description: If this bit is set and the corresponding USB interrupt status bit is set, a HW interrupt is generated on the interrupt line.

field.name: DEV_INT_EN
field.description: If this bit is set and the corresponding USB interrupt status bit is set, a HW interrupt is generated on the interrupt line.

field.name: EP_SET_INT
field.description: If software writes a one to one of these bits, the corresponding USB interrupt status bit is set.

field.name: FRAME_SET_INT
field.description: If software writes a one to one of these bits, the corresponding USB interrupt status bit is set.

field.name: DEV_SET_INT
field.description: If software writes a one to one of these bits, the corresponding USB interrupt status bit is set.

field.name: TOGGLE
field.description: Endpoint data toggle: This field indicates the current value of the data toggle for the corresponding endpoint.

register.name: CAPLENGTH_CHIPID
register.description: This register contains the offset value towards the start of the operational register space and the version number of the IP block

field.name: CAPLENGTH
field.description: Capability Length: This is used as an offset.

field.name: CHIPID
field.description: Chip identification: indicates major and minor revision of the IP: [31:24] = Major revision [23:16] = Minor revision Major revisions used: 0x01: USB2.

field.name: N_PORTS
field.description: This register specifies the number of physical downstream ports implemented on this host controller.

field.name: PPC
field.description: This field indicates whether the host controller implementation includes port power control.

field.name: P_INDICATOR
field.description: This bit indicates whether the ports support port indicator control.

field.name: FRINDEX
field.description: Frame Index: Bits 29 to16 in this register are used for the frame number field in the SOF packet.

register.name: ATLPTD
register.description: Memory base address where ATL PTD0 is stored

field.name: ATL_CUR
field.description: This indicates the current PTD that is used by the hardware when it is processing the ATL list.

field.name: ATL_BASE
field.description: Base address to be used by the hardware to find the start of the ATL list.

register.name: ISOPTD
register.description: Memory base address where ISO PTD0 is stored

field.name: ISO_FIRST
field.description: This indicates the first PTD that is used by the hardware when it is processing the ISO list.

field.name: ISO_BASE
field.description: Base address to be used by the hardware to find the start of the ISO list.

register.name: INTPTD
register.description: Memory base address where INT PTD0 is stored

field.name: INT_FIRST
field.description: This indicates the first PTD that is used by the hardware when it is processing the INT list.

field.name: INT_BASE
field.description: Base address to be used by the hardware to find the start of the INT list.

register.name: DATAPAYLOAD
register.description: Memory base address that indicates the start of the data payload buffers

field.name: DAT_BASE
field.description: Base address to be used by the hardware to find the start of the data payload section.

field.name: HCRESET
field.description: Host Controller Reset: This control bit is used by the software to reset the host controller.

field.name: FLS
field.description: Frame List Size: This field specifies the size of the frame list.

field.name: LHCR
field.description: Light Host Controller Reset: This bit allows the driver software to reset the host controller without affecting the state of the ports.

field.name: PCD
field.description: Port Change Detect: The host controller sets this bit to logic 1 when any port has a change bit transition from a 0 to a one or a Force Port Resume bit transition from a 0 to a 1 as a result of a J-K transition detected on a suspended port. or - the ID pin value changes or - an LPM token has been transmitted to enter LPM L1 suspend state.. Software must write a one to clear the bit

field.name: FLR
field.description: Frame List Rollover: The host controller sets this bit to logic 1 when the frame list index rolls over its maximum value to 0.

field.name: ATL_IRQ
field.description: ATL IRQ: Indicates that an ATL PTD (with I-bit set) was completed.

field.name: ISO_IRQ
field.description: ISO IRQ: Indicates that an ISO PTD (with I-bit set) was completed.

field.name: INT_IRQ
field.description: INT IRQ: Indicates that an INT PTD (with I-bit set) was completed.

field.name: SOF_IRQ
field.description: SOF interrupt: Every time when the host sends a Start of Frame token on the USB bus, this bit is set.

field.name: PCDE
field.description: Port Change Detect Interrupt Enable: 1: enable 0: disable.

field.name: FLRE
field.description: Frame List Rollover Interrupt Enable: 1: enable 0: disable.

field.name: ATL_IRQ_E
field.description: ATL IRQ Enable bit: 1: enable 0: disable.

field.name: ISO_IRQ_E
field.description: ISO IRQ Enable bit: 1: enable 0: disable.

field.name: INT_IRQ_E
field.description: INT IRQ Enable bit: 1: enable 0: disable.

field.name: SOF_E
field.description: SOF Interrupt Enable bit: 1: enable 0: disable.

field.name: CCS
field.description: Current Connect Status: Logic 1 indicates a device is present on the port.

field.name: CSC
field.description: Connect Status Change: Logic 1 means that the value of CCS has changed.

field.name: PEDC
field.description: Port Enabled/Disabled Change: Logic 1 means that the value of PED has changed.

field.name: OCA
field.description: Over-current active: Logic 1 means that this port has an over-current condition.

field.name: OCC
field.description: Over-current change: Logic 1 means that the value of OCA has changed.

field.name: FPR
field.description: Force Port Resume: Logic 1 means resume (K-state) detected or driven on the port.

field.name: SUSP
field.description: Suspend: Logic 1 means port is in the suspend state.Logic 0 means the port is not suspended.

field.name: PR
field.description: Port Reset: Logic 1 means the port is in the reset state.

field.name: SUS_L1
field.description: Suspend using L1 0b = Suspend using L2 1b = Suspend using L1 When this bit is set to a 1 and a non-zero value is specified in the Device Address field, the host controller will generate an LPM Token to enter the L1 state whenever software writes a one to the Suspend bit, as well as L1 exit timing during any device or host-initiated resume.

field.name: LS
field.description: Line Status: This field reflects the current logical levels of the DP (bit 11) and DM (bit 10) signal lines.

field.name: PP
field.description: Port Power: The function of this bit depends on the value of the Port Power Control (PPC) bit in the HCSPARAMS register.

field.name: PIC
field.description: Port Indicator Control : Writing to this field has no effect if the P_INDICATOR bit in the HCSPARAMS register is logic 0.

field.name: PTC
field.description: Port Test Control: A non-zero value indicates that the port is operating in the test mode as indicated by the value.

field.name: PSPD
field.description: Port Speed: 00b: Low-speed 01b: Full-speed 10b: High-speed 11b: Reserved.

field.name: WOO
field.description: Wake on overcurrent enable: Writing this bit to a one enables the port to be sensitive to overcurrent conditions as wake-up events.

field.name: SUS_STAT
field.description: These two bits are used by software to determine whether the most recent L1 suspend request was successful: 00b: Success-state transition was successful (ACK) 01b: Not Yet - Device was unable to enter the L1 state at this time (NYET) 10b: Not supported - Device does not support the L1 state (STALL) 11b: Timeout/Error - Device failed to respond or an error occurred.

field.description: When a bit in the PTD Skip Map is set to logic 1, the corresponding PTD will be skipped, independent of the V bit setting.

register.name: ISOPTDD

field.name: ISO_DONE
field.description: The bit corresponding to a certain PTD will be set to logic 1 as soon as that PTD execution is completed.

register.name: ISOPTDS
register.description: Skip map for each ISO PTD

field.name: ISO_SKIP
field.description: The bit corresponding to a certain PTD will be set to logic 1 as soon as that PTD execution is completed.

register.name: INTPTDD
register.description: Done map for each INT PTD

field.name: INT_DONE
field.description: The bit corresponding to a certain PTD will be set to logic 1 as soon as that PTD execution is completed.

register.name: INTPTDS
register.description: Skip map for each INT PTD

field.name: INT_SKIP
field.description: When a bit in the PTD Skip Map is set to logic 1, the corresponding PTD will be skipped, independent of the V bit setting.

register.name: LASTPTD
register.description: Marks the last PTD in the list for ISO, INT and ATL

field.name: ATL_LAST
field.description: If hardware has reached this PTD and the J bit is not set, it will go to PTD0 as the next PTD to be processed.

field.name: ISO_LAST
field.description: This indicates the last PTD in the ISO list.

field.name: INT_LAST

register.name: PORTMODE
register.description: Controls the port if it is attached to the host block or the device block

field.name: DEV_ENABLE
field.description: If this bit is set to one, the port will behave as a USB device. If this bit is set to zero, the port will be controlled by the USB host block.

enumeratedValue.name: DUAL_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: The SCT operates as two 16-bit counters named COUNTER_L and COUNTER_H.

enumeratedValue.name: UNIFIED_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: The SCT operates as a unified 32-bit counter.

enumeratedValue.name: SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the entire SCT module including the counter(s) and counter prescalers.

enumeratedValue.name: SAMPLED_SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Sampled System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the SCT module, but the counter and prescalers are only enabled to count when the designated edge is detected on the input selected by the CKSEL field. The minimum pulse width on the selected clock-gate input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the high-performance, sampled-clock mode.

enumeratedValue.name: SCT_INPUT_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: SCT Input Clock Mode. The input/edge selected by the CKSEL field clocks the SCT module, including the counters and prescalers, after first being synchronized to the system clock. The minimum pulse width on the clock input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the low-power, sampled-clock mode.

enumeratedValue.name: ASYNCHRONOUS_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Asynchronous Mode. The entire SCT module is clocked directly by the input/edge selected by the CKSEL field. In this mode, the SCT outputs are switched synchronously to the SCT input clock - not the system clock. The input clock rate must be at least half the system clock rate and can be the same or faster than the system clock.

field.name: CKSEL
field.description: SCT clock select. The specific functionality of the designated input/edge is dependent on the CLKMODE bit selection in this register.

field.name: NORELOAD_L
field.description: A 1 in this bit prevents the lower match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers. Setting this bit eliminates the need to write to the reload registers MATCHREL if the match values are fixed. Software can write to set or clear this bit at any time. This bit applies to both the higher and lower registers when the UNIFY bit is set.

field.name: NORELOAD_H
field.description: A 1 in this bit prevents the higher match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers. Setting this bit eliminates the need to write to the reload registers MATCHREL if the match values are fixed. Software can write to set or clear this bit at any time. This bit is not used when the UNIFY bit is set.

field.name: INSYNC
field.description: Synchronization for input N (bit 9 = input 0, bit 10 = input 1,, bit 12 = input 3); all other bits are reserved. A 1 in one of these bits subjects the corresponding input to synchronization to the SCT clock, before it is used to create an event. If an input is known to already be synchronous to the SCT clock, this bit may be set to 0 for faster input response. (Note: The SCT clock is the system clock for CKMODEs 0-2. It is the selected, asynchronous SCT input clock for CKMODE3). Note that the INSYNC field only affects inputs used for event generation. It does not apply to the clock input specified in the CKSEL field.

field.name: AUTOLIMIT_L
field.description: A one in this bit causes a match on match register 0 to be treated as a de-facto LIMIT condition without the need to define an associated event. As with any LIMIT event, this automatic limit causes the counter to be cleared to zero in unidirectional mode or to change the direction of count in bi-directional mode. Software can write to set or clear this bit at any time. This bit applies to both the higher and lower registers when the UNIFY bit is set.

field.name: AUTOLIMIT_H
field.description: A one in this bit will cause a match on match register 0 to be treated as a de-facto LIMIT condition without the need to define an associated event. As with any LIMIT event, this automatic limit causes the counter to be cleared to zero in unidirectional mode or to change the direction of count in bi-directional mode. Software can write to set or clear this bit at any time. This bit is not used when the UNIFY bit is set.

field.name: DOWN_L
field.description: This bit is 1 when the L or unified counter is counting down. Hardware sets this bit when the counter is counting up, counter limit occurs, and BIDIR = 1.Hardware clears this bit when the counter is counting down and a limit condition occurs or when the counter reaches 0.

field.name: STOP_L
field.description: When this bit is 1 and HALT is 0, the L or unified counter does not run, but I/O events related to the counter can occur. If a designated start event occurs, this bit is cleared and counting resumes.

field.name: HALT_L
field.description: When this bit is 1, the L or unified counter does not run and no events can occur. A reset sets this bit. When the HALT_L bit is one, the STOP_L bit is cleared. It is possible to remove the halt condition while keeping the SCT in the stop condition (not running) with a single write to this register to simultaneously clear the HALT bit and set the STOP bit. Once set, only software can clear this bit to restore counter operation. This bit is set on reset.

field.name: CLRCTR_L
field.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the L or unified counter. This bit always reads as 0.

field.name: BIDIR_L
field.description: L or unified counter direction select

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The counter counts up to a limit condition, then is cleared to zero.

enumeratedValue.name: UP_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Up-down. The counter counts up to a limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.

field.name: PRE_L
field.description: Specifies the factor by which the SCT clock is prescaled to produce the L or unified counter clock. The counter clock is clocked at the rate of the SCT clock divided by PRE_L+1. Clear the counter (by writing a 1 to the CLRCTR bit) whenever changing the PRE value.

field.name: DOWN_H
field.description: This bit is 1 when the H counter is counting down. Hardware sets this bit when the counter is counting, a counter limit condition occurs, and BIDIR is 1. Hardware clears this bit when the counter is counting down and a limit condition occurs or when the counter reaches 0.

field.name: STOP_H
field.description: When this bit is 1 and HALT is 0, the H counter does not, run but I/O events related to the counter can occur. If such an event matches the mask in the Start register, this bit is cleared and counting resumes.

field.name: HALT_H
field.description: When this bit is 1, the H counter does not run and no events can occur. A reset sets this bit. When the HALT_H bit is one, the STOP_H bit is cleared. It is possible to remove the halt condition while keeping the SCT in the stop condition (not running) with a single write to this register to simultaneously clear the HALT bit and set the STOP bit. Once set, this bit can only be cleared by software to restore counter operation. This bit is set on reset.

field.name: CLRCTR_H
field.description: Writing a 1 to this bit clears the H counter. This bit always reads as 0.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: The H counter counts up to its limit condition, then is cleared to zero.

enumeratedValue.name: UP_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: The H counter counts up to its limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.

field.name: PRE_H
field.description: Specifies the factor by which the SCT clock is prescaled to produce the H counter clock. The counter clock is clocked at the rate of the SCT clock divided by PRELH+1. Clear the counter (by writing a 1 to the CLRCTR bit) whenever changing the PRE value.

field.name: LIMMSK_L
field.description: If bit n is one, event n is used as a counter limit for the L or unified counter (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: LIMMSK_H
field.description: If bit n is one, event n is used as a counter limit for the H counter (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: HALTMSK_L
field.description: If bit n is one, event n sets the HALT_L bit in the CTRL register (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: HALTMSK_H
field.description: If bit n is one, event n sets the HALT_H bit in the CTRL register (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: STOPMSK_L
field.description: If bit n is one, event n sets the STOP_L bit in the CTRL register (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: STOPMSK_H
field.description: If bit n is one, event n sets the STOP_H bit in the CTRL register (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: STARTMSK_L
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the STOP_L bit in the CTRL register (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: STARTMSK_H
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the STOP_H bit in the CTRL register (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: CTR_L
field.description: When UNIFY = 0, read or write the 16-bit L counter value. When UNIFY = 1, read or write the lower 16 bits of the 32-bit unified counter.

field.name: CTR_H
field.description: When UNIFY = 0, read or write the 16-bit H counter value. When UNIFY = 1, read or write the upper 16 bits of the 32-bit unified counter.

field.name: REGMOD_L
field.description: Each bit controls one match/capture register (register 0 = bit 0, register 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of match/captures in this SCT. 0 = register operates as match register. 1 = register operates as capture register.

field.name: REGMOD_H
field.description: Each bit controls one match/capture register (register 0 = bit 16, register 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of match/captures in this SCT. 0 = register operates as match registers. 1 = register operates as capture registers.

field.name: OUT
field.description: Writing a 1 to bit n forces the corresponding output HIGH. Writing a 0 forces the corresponding output LOW (output 0 = bit 0, output 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of outputs in this SCT.

field.name: SETCLR3
field.description: Set/clear operation on output 3. Value 0x3 is reserved. Do not program this value.

enumeratedValue.name: INDEPENDENT
enumeratedValue.description: Set and clear do not depend on the direction of any counter.

enumeratedValue.name: L_REVERSED
enumeratedValue.description: Set and clear are reversed when counter L or the unified counter is counting down.

enumeratedValue.name: H_REVERSED
enumeratedValue.description: Set and clear are reversed when counter H is counting down. Do not use if UNIFY = 1.

field.name: DEV_0
field.description: If bit n is one, event n triggers DMA request 0 (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: DRL0
field.description: A 1 in this bit triggers DMA request 0 when it loads the MATCH_L/Unified registers from the RELOAD_L/Unified registers.

field.name: DRQ0
field.description: This read-only bit indicates the state of DMA Request 0. Note that if the related DMA channel is enabled and properly set up, it is unlikely that software will see this flag, it will be cleared rapidly by the DMA service. The flag remaining set could point to an issue with DMA setup.

field.name: DEV_1
field.description: If bit n is one, event n triggers DMA request 1 (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: DRL1
field.description: A 1 in this bit triggers DMA request 1 when it loads the Match L/Unified registers from the Reload L/Unified registers.

field.name: DRQ1
field.description: This read-only bit indicates the state of DMA Request 1. Note that if the related DMA channel is enabled and properly set up, it is unlikely that software will see this flag, it will be cleared rapidly by the DMA service. The flag remaining set could point to an issue with DMA setup.

field.name: IEN
field.description: The SCT requests an interrupt when bit n of this register and the event flag register are both one (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: FLAG
field.description: Bit n is one if event n has occurred since reset or a 1 was last written to this bit (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: NCEN
field.description: The SCT requests an interrupt when bit n of this register and the SCT conflict flag register are both one (output 0 = bit 0, output 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of outputs in this SCT.

field.name: NCFLAG
field.description: Bit n is one if a no-change conflict event occurred on output n since reset or a 1 was last written to this bit (output 0 = bit 0, output 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of outputs in this SCT.

field.name: BUSERRL
field.description: The most recent bus error from this SCT involved writing CTR L/Unified, STATE L/Unified, MATCH L/Unified, or the Output register when the L/U counter was not halted. A word write to certain L and H registers can be half successful and half unsuccessful.

field.name: BUSERRH
field.description: The most recent bus error from this SCT involved writing CTR H, STATE H, MATCH H, or the Output register when the H counter was not halted.

register.name: CAP0
register.description: SCT capture register of capture channel

field.name: CAPn_L
field.description: When UNIFY = 0, read the 16-bit counter value at which this register was last captured. When UNIFY = 1, read the lower 16 bits of the 32-bit value at which this register was last captured.

field.name: CAPn_H
field.description: When UNIFY = 0, read the 16-bit counter value at which this register was last captured. When UNIFY = 1, read the upper 16 bits of the 32-bit value at which this register was last captured.

register.name: MATCH0
register.description: SCT match value register of match channels

field.name: MATCHn_L
field.description: When UNIFY = 0, read or write the 16-bit value to be compared to the L counter. When UNIFY = 1, read or write the lower 16 bits of the 32-bit value to be compared to the unified counter.

field.name: MATCHn_H
field.description: When UNIFY = 0, read or write the 16-bit value to be compared to the H counter. When UNIFY = 1, read or write the upper 16 bits of the 32-bit value to be compared to the unified counter.

field.name: STATEMSKn
field.description: If bit m is one, event n happens in state m of the counter selected by the HEVENT bit (n = event number, m = state number; state 0 = bit 0, state 1= bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of states in this SCT.

field.name: MATCHSEL
field.description: Selects the Match register associated with this event (if any). A match can occur only when the counter selected by the HEVENT bit is running.

field.name: HEVENT
field.description: Select L/H counter. Do not set this bit if UNIFY = 1.

enumeratedValue.name: L_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: Selects the L state and the L match register selected by MATCHSEL.

enumeratedValue.name: H_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: Selects the H state and the H match register selected by MATCHSEL.

enumeratedValue.name: INPUT
enumeratedValue.description: Selects the inputs selected by IOSEL.

enumeratedValue.name: OUTPUT
enumeratedValue.description: Selects the outputs selected by IOSEL.

field.name: IOSEL
field.description: Selects the input or output signal number associated with this event (if any). Do not select an input in this register if CKMODE is 1x. In this case the clock input is an implicit ingredient of every event.

field.name: IOCOND
field.description: Selects the I/O condition for event n. (The detection of edges on outputs lag the conditions that switch the outputs by one SCT clock). In order to guarantee proper edge/state detection, an input must have a minimum pulse width of at least one SCT clock period .

field.name: COMBMODE
field.description: Selects how the specified match and I/O condition are used and combined.

enumeratedValue.name: OR
enumeratedValue.description: OR. The event occurs when either the specified match or I/O condition occurs.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: MATCH. Uses the specified match only.

enumeratedValue.name: IO
enumeratedValue.description: IO. Uses the specified I/O condition only.

enumeratedValue.name: AND
enumeratedValue.description: AND. The event occurs when the specified match and I/O condition occur simultaneously.

field.name: STATELD
field.description: This bit controls how the STATEV value modifies the state selected by HEVENT when this event is the highest-numbered event occurring for that state.

enumeratedValue.name: ADD
enumeratedValue.description: STATEV value is added into STATE (the carry-out is ignored).

enumeratedValue.name: LOAD
enumeratedValue.description: STATEV value is loaded into STATE.

field.name: STATEV
field.description: This value is loaded into or added to the state selected by HEVENT, depending on STATELD, when this event is the highest-numbered event occurring for that state. If STATELD and STATEV are both zero, there is no change to the STATE value.

field.name: MATCHMEM
field.description: If this bit is one and the COMBMODE field specifies a match component to the triggering of this event, then a match is considered to be active whenever the counter value is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO the value specified in the match register when counting up, LESS THEN OR EQUAL TO the match value when counting down. If this bit is zero, a match is only be active during the cycle when the counter is equal to the match value.

field.name: DIRECTION
field.description: Direction qualifier for event generation. This field only applies when the counters are operating in BIDIR mode. If BIDIR = 0, the SCT ignores this field. Value 0x3 is reserved.

enumeratedValue.name: DIRECTION_INDEPENDENT
enumeratedValue.description: Direction independent. This event is triggered regardless of the count direction.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTING_UP
enumeratedValue.description: Counting up. This event is triggered only during up-counting when BIDIR = 1.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTING_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Counting down. This event is triggered only during down-counting when BIDIR = 1.

field.name: SET
field.description: A 1 in bit m selects event m to set output n (or clear it if SETCLRn = 0x1 or 0x2) output 0 = bit 0, output 1 = bit 1, etc. The number of bits = number of events in this SCT. When the counter is used in bi-directional mode, it is possible to reverse the action specified by the output set and clear registers when counting down, See the OUTPUTCTRL register.

field.name: CLR
field.description: A 1 in bit m selects event m to clear output n (or set it if SETCLRn = 0x1 or 0x2) event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc. The number of bits = number of events in this SCT. When the counter is used in bi-directional mode, it is possible to reverse the action specified by the output set and clear registers when counting down, See the OUTPUTCTRL register.

register.name: OUTBASE
register.description: Base address register for output region

field.name: outbase
field.description: Base address register for the output region

register.name: TMPBASE
register.description: Base address register for temp region

field.name: tmpbase
field.description: Base address register for the temporary region

register.name: INABASE
register.description: Base address register for input A region

field.name: inabase
field.description: Base address register for the input A region

field.name: ina_scaler
field.description: Input A Scaler value (for scaled 'q31' formats)

register.name: INBBASE
register.description: Base address register for input B region

field.name: inbbase
field.description: Base address register for the input B region

field.name: inb_scaler
field.description: Input B Scaler value (for scaled 'q31' formats)

field.name: decode_machine
field.description: 0 : Coprocessor , 1 : matrix , 2 : fft , 3 : fir , 4 : stat , 5 : cordic , 6 -15 : NA

field.name: inst_busy
field.description: Instruction busy signal when high indicates processing is on

field.name: inst_length
field.description: Length register. When FIR : fir_xlength = inst_length[15:0] , fir_tlength = inst_len[31:16]. When MTX : rows_a = inst_length[4:0] , cols_a = inst_length[12:8] , cols_b = inst_length[20:16]

field.name: inst_misc
field.description: Misc register. For Matrix : Used for scale factor

register.name: ERRSTAT
register.description: Read/Write register where error statuses are captured (sticky)

field.name: intr_oflow
field.description: 1 : Enable interrupt on Floating point overflow

field.name: intr_nan
field.description: 1 : Enable interrupt on Floating point NaN

field.name: intr_fixed
field.description: 1: Enable interrupt on Fixed point Overflow

field.name: intr_berr
field.description: 1: Enable interrupt on AHBM Buss Error

field.name: event_oflow
field.description: 1 : Enable event trigger on Floating point overflow

field.name: event_nan
field.description: 1 : Enable event trigger on Floating point NaN

field.name: event_fixed
field.description: 1: Enable event trigger on Fixed point Overflow

field.name: event_uflow
field.description: 1 : Enable event trigger on Subnormal truncation

field.name: event_berr
field.description: 1: Enable event trigger on AHBM Buss Error

field.name: event_comp
field.description: 1: Enable event trigger on instruction completion

field.name: intr_stat
field.description: Intr status ( 1 bit to indicate interrupt captured, 0 means no new interrupt), write any value will clear this bit

register.name: CTRL0
register.description: Contains the offsets of AB and CD in the RAM.

field.name: ABBPAIR
field.description: Which bank-pair the offset ABOFF is within. This must be 0 if only 2-up

field.name: ABOFF
field.description: Word or DWord Offset of AB values, with B at [2]=0 and A at [2]=1 as far as the code sees (normally will be an interleaved bank so only sequential to AHB). Word offset only allowed if 32 bit operation. Ideally not in the same RAM as the CD values if 4-up

field.name: CDBPAIR
field.description: Which bank-pair the offset CDOFF is within. This must be 0 if only 2-up

field.name: CDOFF
field.description: Word or DWord Offset of CD, with D at [2]=0 and C at [2]=1 as far as the code sees (normally will be an interleaved bank so only sequential to AHB). Word offset only allowed if 32 bit operation. Ideally not in the same RAM as the AB values

register.name: CTRL1
register.description: Contains the opcode mode, iteration count, and result offset (in RAM) and also launches the accelerator. Note: with CP version: CTRL0 and CRTL1 can be written in one go with MCRR.

field.name: ITER
field.description: Iteration counter. Is number_cycles - 1. write 0 means Does one cycle - does not iterate.

field.name: MODE
field.description: Operation mode to perform. write 0 means Accelerator is inactive. write others means accelerator is active.

field.name: RESBPAIR
field.description: Which bank-pair the offset RESOFF is within. This must be 0 if only 2-up. Ideally this is not the same bank as ABBPAIR (when 4-up supported)

field.name: RESOFF
field.description: Word or DWord Offset of result. Word offset only allowed if 32 bit operation. Ideally not in the same RAM as the AB and CD values

field.name: CSKIP
field.description: Skip rules on Carry if needed. This operation will be skipped based on Carry value (from previous operation) if not 0:

enumeratedValue.name: SET_AND_SKIP
enumeratedValue.description: Set CTRLOFF to CDOFF and Skip

register.name: STATUS
register.description: Indicates operational status and would contain the carry bit if used.

field.name: DONE
field.description: Indicates if the accelerator has finished an operation. Write 1 to clear, or write CTRL1 to clear.

field.name: CARRY
field.description: Last carry value if operation produced a carry bit

field.name: BUSY
field.description: Indicates if the accelerator is busy performing an operation

field.name: DONE
field.description: Set if the accelerator should interrupt when done.

field.name: DONE
field.description: Written to clear an interrupt set with INTENSET.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: If written 1, do not Interrupt when done

register.name: INTSTAT
register.description: Interrupt status bits (mask of INTENSET and STATUS)

field.name: DONE
field.description: If set, interrupt is caused by accelerator being done.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_CAUSED
enumeratedValue.description: Not caused by accelerator being done

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to be fed into Multiplier. Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to be fed into Multiplier. Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to be fed into Multiplier. Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to be fed into Multiplier. Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to hold working result (from multiplier, adder/xor, etc). Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to hold working result (from multiplier, adder/xor, etc). Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to hold working result (from multiplier, adder/xor, etc). Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: REG_VALUE
field.description: Register to hold working result (from multiplier, adder/xor, etc). Is not normally written or read by application, but is available when accelerator not busy.

field.name: MASK
field.description: Mask to apply as side channel countermeasure. 0: No mask to be used. N: Mask to XOR onto values

field.name: MASK
field.description: Mask to apply as side channel countermeasure. 0: No mask to be used. N: Mask to XOR onto values

field.name: LOCK
field.description: Reads back with security level locked to, or 0. Writes as 0 to unlock, 1 to lock.

field.name: KEY
field.description: Must be written as 0x73D to change the register.

enumeratedValue.name: KWY_VALUE
enumeratedValue.description: If set during write, will allow lock or unlock

register.name: CTRL
register.description: Control register to enable and operate Hash and Crypto

field.name: Mode
field.description: The operational mode to use, or 0 if none. Note that the CONFIG register will indicate if specific modes beyond SHA1 and SHA2-256 are available.

enumeratedValue.name: AES
enumeratedValue.description: AES if available (see also CRYPTCFG register for more controls)

enumeratedValue.name: ICB_AES
enumeratedValue.description: ICB-AES if available (see also CRYPTCFG register for more controls)

field.name: New_Hash
field.description: Written with 1 when starting a new Hash/Crypto. It self clears. Note that the WAITING Status bit will clear for a cycle during the initialization from New=1.

enumeratedValue.name: START
enumeratedValue.description: Starts a new Hash/Crypto and initializes the Digest/Result.

field.name: RELOAD
field.description: If 1, allows the SHA RELOAD registers to be used. This is used to save a partial Hash Digest (e.g. when need to run AES) and then reload it later for continuation.

enumeratedValue.name: RELOAD
enumeratedValue.description: Allow RELOAD registers to be used.

field.name: DMA_I
field.description: Written with 1 to use DMA to fill INDATA. If Hash, will request from DMA for 16 words and then will process the Hash. If Cryptographic, it will load as many words as needed, including key if not already loaded. It will then request again. Normal model is that the DMA interrupts the processor when its length expires. Note that if the processor will write the key and optionally IV, it should not enable this until it has done so. Otherwise, the DMA will be expected to load those for the 1st block (when needed).

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_USED
enumeratedValue.description: DMA is not used. Processor writes the necessary words when WAITING is set (interrupts), unless AHB Master is used.

enumeratedValue.name: PUSH
enumeratedValue.description: DMA will push in the data.

field.name: DMA_O
field.description: Written to 1 to use DMA to drain the digest/output. If both DMA_I and DMA_O are set, the DMA has to know to switch direction and the locations. This can be used for crypto uses.

enumeratedValue.name: NOTUSED
enumeratedValue.description: DMA is not used. Processor reads the digest/output in response to DIGEST interrupt.

field.name: HASHSWPB
field.description: If 1, will swap bytes in the word for SHA hashing. The default is byte order (so LSB is 1st byte) but this allows swapping to MSB is 1st such as is shown in SHS spec. For cryptographic swapping, see the CRYPTCFG register.

field.name: WAITING
field.description: If 1, the block is waiting for more data to process.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_WAITING
enumeratedValue.description: Not waiting for data - may be disabled or may be busy. Note that for cryptographic uses, this is not set if IsLast is set nor will it set until at least 1 word is read of the output.

enumeratedValue.name: WAITING
enumeratedValue.description: Waiting for data to be written in (16 words)

field.name: DIGEST
field.description: For Hash, if 1 then a DIGEST is ready and waiting and there is no active next block already started. For Cryptographic uses, this will be set for each block processed, indicating OUTDATA (and OUTDATA2 if larger output) contains the next value to read out. This is cleared when any data is written, when New is written, for Cryptographic uses when the last word is read out, or when the block is disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: READY
enumeratedValue.description: Digest is ready. Application may read it or may write more data

field.name: ERROR
field.description: If 1, an error occurred. For normal uses, this is due to an attempted overrun: INDATA was written when it was not appropriate. For Master cases, this is an AHB bus error; the COUNT field will indicate which block it was on.

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: An error occurred since last cleared (written 1 to clear).

field.name: NEEDKEY
field.description: Indicates the block wants the key to be written in (set along with WAITING)

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_NEED
enumeratedValue.description: No Key is needed and writes will not be treated as Key

enumeratedValue.name: NEED
enumeratedValue.description: Key is needed and INDATA/ALIAS will be accepted as Key. Will also set WAITING.

field.name: NEEDIV
field.description: Indicates the block wants an IV/NONE to be written in (set along with WAITING)

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_NEED
enumeratedValue.description: No IV/Nonce is needed, either because written already or because not needed.

enumeratedValue.name: NEED
enumeratedValue.description: IV/Nonce is needed and INDATA/ALIAS will be accepted as IV/Nonce. Will also set WAITING.

field.name: ICBIDX
field.description: If ICB-AES is selected, then reads as the ICB index count based on ICBSTRM (from CRYPTCFG). That is, if 3 bits of ICBSTRM, then this will count from 0 to 7 and then back to 0. On 0, it has to compute the full ICB, quicker when not 0.

register.name: INTENSET
register.description: Write 1 to enable interrupts; reads back with which are set.

field.name: WAITING
field.description: Indicates if should interrupt when waiting for data input.

field.name: DIGEST
field.description: Indicates if should interrupt when Digest (or Outdata) is ready (completed a hash/crypto or completed a full sequence).

enumeratedValue.name: NO_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: Will not interrupt when Digest is ready

enumeratedValue.name: INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: Will interrupt when Digest is ready. Interrupt cleared by writing more data, starting a new Hash, or disabling (done).

field.name: ERROR
field.description: Indicates if should interrupt on an ERROR (as defined in Status)

register.name: MEMCTRL
register.description: Setup Master to access memory (if available)

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_USED
enumeratedValue.description: Mastering is not used and the normal DMA or Interrupt based model is used with INDATA.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Mastering is enabled and DMA and INDATA should not be used.

field.name: COUNT
field.description: Number of 512-bit (128-bit if AES, except 1st block which may include key and IV) blocks to copy starting at MEMADDR. This register will decrement after each block is copied, ending in 0. For Hash, the DIGEST interrupt will occur when it reaches 0. Fro AES, the DIGEST/OUTDATA interrupt will occur on ever block. If a bus error occurs, it will stop with this field set to the block that failed. 0:Done - nothing to process. 1 to 2K: Number of 512-bit (or 128bit) blocks to hash.

register.name: MEMADDR
register.description: Address to start memory access from (if available).

field.name: BASE
field.description: Address base to start copying from, word aligned (so bits 1:0 must be 0). This field will advance as it processes the words. If it fails with a bus error, the register will contain the failing word. N:Address in Flash or RAM space; RAM only as mapped in this part. May also be able to address SPIFI.

register.name: INDATA
register.description: Input of 16 words at a time to load up buffer.

field.name: DATA
field.description: Write next word in little-endian form. The hash requires big endian word data, but this block swaps the bytes automatically. That is, SHA assumes the data coming in is treated as bytes (e.g. "abcd") and since the ARM core will treat "abcd" as a word as 0x64636261, the block will swap the word to restore into big endian.

field.name: DATA
field.description: Write next word in little-endian form. The hash requires big endian word data, but this block swaps the bytes automatically. That is, SHA assumes the data coming in is treated as bytes (e.g. "abcd") and since the ARM core will treat "abcd" as a word as 0x64636261, the block will swap the word to restore into big endian.

field.name: DIGEST
field.description: One word of the Digest or output. Note that only 1st 4 are populated for AES and 1st 5 are populated for SHA1.

register.name: CRYPTCFG
register.description: Crypto settings for AES and Salsa and ChaCha

field.name: MSW1ST_OUT
field.description: If 1, OUTDATA0 will be read Most significant word 1st for AES. Else it will be read in normal little endian - Least significant word 1st. Note: only if allowed by configuration.

field.name: SWAPKEY
field.description: If 1, will Swap the key input (bytes in each word).

field.name: SWAPDAT
field.description: If 1, will SWAP the data and IV inputs (bytes in each word).

field.name: MSW1ST
field.description: If 1, load of key, IV, and data is MSW 1st for AES. Else, the words are little endian. Note: only if allowed by configuration.

field.name: AESMODE
field.description: AES Cipher mode to use if plain AES

enumeratedValue.name: CTR
enumeratedValue.description: CTR mode (see details on IV/nonce). See also AESCTRPOS.

field.name: AESDECRYPT
field.description: AES ECB direction. Only encryption used if CTR mode or manual modes such as CFB

field.name: AESSECRET
field.description: Selects the Hidden Secret key vs. User key, if provided. If security levels are used, only the highest level is permitted to select this.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL_WAY
enumeratedValue.description: User key provided in normal way

enumeratedValue.name: HIDDEN_WAY
enumeratedValue.description: Secret key provided in hidden way by HW

field.name: AESCTRPOS
field.description: Halfword position of 16b counter in IV if AESMODE is CTR (position is fixed for Salsa and ChaCha). Only supports 16b counter, so application must control any additional bytes if using more. The 16-bit counter is read from the IV and incremented by 1 each time. Any other use CTR should use ECB directly and do its own XOR and so on.

field.name: STREAMLAST
field.description: Is 1 if last stream block. If not 1, then the engine will compute the next "hash".

field.name: ICBSZ
field.description: This sets the ICB size between 32 and 128 bits, using the following rules. Note that the counter is assumed to occupy the low order bits of the IV.

enumeratedValue.name: BITS_32
enumeratedValue.description: 32 bits of the IV/ctr are used (from 127:96)

enumeratedValue.name: BITS_64
enumeratedValue.description: 64 bits of the IV/ctr are used (from 127:64)

enumeratedValue.name: BITS_96
enumeratedValue.description: 96 bits of the IV/ctr are used (from 127:32)

enumeratedValue.name: BIT_128
enumeratedValue.description: All 128 bits of the IV/ctr are used

field.name: ICBSTRM
field.description: The size of the ICB-AES stream that can be pushed before needing to compute a new IV/ctr (counter start). This optimizes the performance of the stream of blocks after the 1st.

register.name: CONFIG
register.description: Returns the configuration of this block in this chip - indicates what services are available.

field.name: DUAL
field.description: 1 if 2 x 512 bit buffers, 0 if only 1 x 512 bit

register.name: LOCK
register.description: Lock register allows locking to the current security level or unlocking by the lock holding level.

field.name: SECLOCK
field.description: Write 1 to secure-lock this block (if running in a security state). Write 0 to unlock. If locked already, may only write if at same or higher security level as lock. Reads as: 0 if unlocked, else 1, 2, 3 to indicate security level it is locked at. NOTE: this and ID are the only readable registers if locked and current state is lower than lock level.

enumeratedValue.name: UNLOCK
enumeratedValue.description: Unlocks, so block is open to all. But, AHB Master will only issue non-secure requests.

enumeratedValue.name: LOCK
enumeratedValue.description: Locks to the current security level. AHB Master will issue requests at this level.

field.name: PATTERN
field.description: Must write 0xA75 to change lock state. A75:Pattern needed to change bits 1:0

register.name: PRNG_SEED
register.description: PRNG random seed input value used as an entropy source

field.name: PRNG_SEED
field.description: Random input value used as an entropy source

field.name: PRNG_OUT
field.description: Random output value from the PRNG. The PRNG output is disabled and this register is set to 0x00000000 when the AES is enabled.

field.name: INTID
field.description: Interrupt ID of the interrupt to trigger, in the range 0-479.

register.name: AIRCR
register.description: Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register

field.name: VECTCLRACTIVE
field.description: Reserved for Debug use. This bit reads as 0. When writing to the register you must write 0 to this bit, otherwise behavior is UNPREDICTABLE. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: SYSRESETREQ
field.description: System reset request. This bit allows software or a debugger to request a system reset. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW if SYSRESETREQS is 0. When SYSRESETREQS is set to 1, from Non-secure state this bit acts as RAZ/WI.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_REQUEST
enumeratedValue.description: Do not request a system reset.

field.name: SYSRESETREQS
field.description: System reset request, Secure state only. The value of this bit defines whether the SYSRESETREQ bit is functional for Non-secure use. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure State and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is available to both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is only available to Secure state.

field.name: PRIGROUP
field.description: Interrupt priority grouping field. This field determines the split of group priority from subpriority. This bit is banked between Security states

field.name: BFHFNMINS
field.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI Non-secure enable. The value of this bit defines whether BusFault and NMI exceptions are Non-secure, and whether exceptions target the Non-secure HardFault exception. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure-state and RO from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI are Secure.

enumeratedValue.name: NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault and NMI are Non-secure and exceptions can target Non-secure HardFault.

field.name: PRIS
field.description: Prioritize Secure exceptions. The value of this bit defines whether Secure exception priority boosting is enabled. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure state and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SAME_PRIORITY
enumeratedValue.description: Priority ranges of Secure and Non-secure exceptions are identical

field.name: ENDIANNESS
field.description: Data endianness bit. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: VECTKEY
field.description: Register key: Reads as 0xFA05. On writes, write 0x5FA to VECTKEY, otherwise the write is ignored. This Field is not banked between Security states.

register.name: SCR
register.description: The SCR controls features of entry to and exit from low-power state.

field.name: SLEEPONEXIT
field.description: Indicates sleep-on-exit when returning from Handler mode to Thread mode. Setting this bit to 1 enables an interrupt driven application to avoid returning to an empty main application. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Do not sleep when returning to Thread mode.

enumeratedValue.name: SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Enter sleep, or deep sleep, on return from an ISR

field.name: SLEEPDEEP
field.description: Controls whether the processor uses sleep or deep sleep as its low-power mode. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: SLEEPDEEPS
field.description: Controls whether the SLEEPDEEP bit is only accessible from the Secure state. This bit in only accessible from the Secure state, and behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Nonsecure state. This bit is not banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit is accessible from both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Non-secure state.

field.name: SEVONPEND
field.description: Send Event on Pending bit. When an event or interrupt enters pending state, the event signal wakes up the processor from WFE. If the processor is not waiting for an event, the event is registered and affects the next WFE. The processor also wakes up on execution of an SEV instruction or an external event. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Only enabled interrupts or events can wakeup the processor, disabled interrupts are excluded.

enumeratedValue.name: INCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled events and all interrupts, including disabled interrupts, can wakeup the processor

register.name: TYPE
register.description: The MPU Type Register indicates how many regions the MPU support. Software can use it to determine if the processor implements an MPU.

field.name: SEPARATE
field.description: Indicates support for separate instruction and data address maps. RAZ. Armv8-M only supports a unified MPU

field.name: DREGION
field.description: Number of regions supported by the MPU. If this field reads-as-zero the processor does not implement an MPU.

field.name: HFNMIENA
field.description: Enables the operation of MPU during HardFault and NMI handlers

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MPU is disabled during HardFault and NMI handlers.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: The MPU is enabled during HardFault and NMI handlers.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disables the default memory map. Any instruction or data access that does not access a defined region faults.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enables the default memory map as a background region for privileged accesses.

field.name: REGION
field.description: Indicates the memory region accessed by MPU_RBAR and MPU_RASR.

field.name: XN
field.description: The XN bit is an Execute Never bit, that indicates whether the processor can execute instructions from the region.

enumeratedValue.name: EXECUTE
enumeratedValue.description: Execution is only permitted if read permitted.

field.name: AP
field.description: The AP[2:0] bits indicate the access and privilege properties of the region.

field.name: SH
field.description: For Normal memory regions, the S bit indicates whether the region is shareable. For Strongly-ordered and Device memory, the S bit is ignored.

field.name: BASE
field.description: Contains bits[31:5] of the lower inclusive limit of the selected MPU memory region. This value is zero extended to provide the base address to be checked against.

field.name: ATTRINDX
field.description: Attribute index. Associates a set of attributes in the MPU_MAIR0 and MPU_MAIR1 fields.

field.name: LIMIT
field.description: Limit address. Contains bits[31:5] of the upper inclusive limit of the selected MPU memory region. This value is postfixed with 0x1F to provide the limit address to be checked against.

field.name: XN
field.description: The XN bit is an Execute Never bit, that indicates whether the processor can execute instructions from the region.

field.name: ATTR1
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 1.

field.name: ATTR2
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 2.

field.name: ATTR3

field.name: ATTR4

field.name: ATTR5

field.name: ATTR6

field.name: ATTR7

field.name: ENABLE
field.description: Enable. Enables the SAU. This bit is RAZ/WI when the Security Extension is implemented without an SAU region.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURED_MEMORY
enumeratedValue.description: Memory is marked as Secure and is not Non-secure callable.

field.name: SREGION
field.description: SAU regions. The number of implemented SAU regions.

register.name: RNR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Number Register

register.name: RBAR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Base Address Register

field.name: BADDR
field.description: Base address. Holds bits[31:5] of the base address for the selected SAU region. Bits[4:0] of the base address are defined as 0x00.

register.name: RLAR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Limit Address Register

field.name: NSC
field.description: Non-secure callable. Controls whether Non-secure state is permitted to execute an SG instruction from this region.

field.name: LADDR
field.description: Limit address. Holds bits[31:5] of the limit address for the selected SAU region. Bits[4:0] of the limit address are defined as 0x1F.

field.name: ADDRESS
field.description: When the SFARVALID bit of the SFSR is set to 1, this field holds the address of an access that caused an SAU violation.
